Introduce a file-based (flock) process-level mutex to serialize access to the JSONL data file so concurrent processes don't cause merge races or data corruption.

## Problem
Multiple CLI processes or the API server can simultaneously read/modify the shared worklog-data.jsonl file. The exportToJsonl() method in database.ts performs a read-merge-write cycle that is susceptible to TOCTOU races. refreshFromJsonlIfNewer() can interleave with exports from other processes. The sync command performs fetch-merge-import-export-push without any lock.

## User Story
As a developer using Worklog in a team environment, I want concurrent wl commands to safely serialize their access to the shared JSONL data file so that no data is lost or corrupted due to race conditions.

## Implementation Approach
- Create a new src/file-lock.ts module that implements file-based locking using Node.js fs.open with O_EXCL (advisory lock file)
- The lock file will be placed alongside the JSONL data file (e.g., worklog-data.jsonl.lock)
- Provide withFileLock(lockPath, fn) helper that acquires the lock, runs the callback, and releases it (with proper cleanup on error)
- Include retry logic with configurable timeout and backoff for waiting on a held lock
- Include stale lock detection (process ID recorded in lock file, checked on acquisition failure)
- Integrate locking into WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl() and WorklogDatabase.refreshFromJsonlIfNewer()
- Integrate locking into the sync, import, and export command handlers
- Write tests that simulate concurrent processes to validate serialization

## Acceptance Criteria
- A new src/file-lock.ts module exists with withFileLock() and related helpers
- Import/export/sync operations acquire the lock before running and release after
- Stale locks (from crashed processes) are detected and cleaned up
- Tests simulate concurrent processes to validate serialization
- All existing tests continue to pass
- The lock does not introduce noticeable latency for single-process usage
data.title: Process-level mutex for import/export/sync

Summary:
Write a feature request for the `wl` team to add global plugin directory scanning at `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/.worklog/plugins/`.

Requester: SorraAgents (SA-0MLRSH3EU14UT79F)

Parent epic: SA-0MLRONXRF1N732R1 (this item is a blocking dependency for that epic)

User story:
As an operator running multiple projects on the same host, I want `wl` to discover plugins installed in a global directory (`~/.config/opencode/.worklog/plugins/`) in addition to the project-local `.worklog/plugins/` directory, so that I can install a plugin once and have it available across all projects.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Feature request work item exists as a child of SA-0MLRONXRF1N732R1.
2. Specifies the desired resolution order: project-local plugins load first, then global (project overrides global).
3. Specifies fallback behaviour when both directories contain a plugin with the same filename (project-local wins).
4. Specifies that `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` should be respected for the global path.
5. Identifies that this blocks the parent epic from full completion (no interim workaround is being used).
6. Includes a user story from the operator perspective.

Desired behaviour / specification:
- `wl` scans for plugins in both locations, with this resolution order:
  1. `<project>/.worklog/plugins/` (project-local, highest priority)
  2. `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode/.worklog/plugins/` (global, lower priority)
- If the same plugin filename exists in both directories, the project-local version takes precedence.
- `wl` should respect `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` when resolving the global path; if `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset, fallback to `$HOME/.config`.
- Optionally expose a configuration key (e.g. `pluginDirs`) to allow custom paths, but the two defaults above must work with zero configuration.

Motivation:
- SA-0MLRONXRF1N732R1 moves AMPA plugin installation to the global directory. Without `wl` scanning the global directory, globally installed plugins remain invisible to `wl`.
- Enables a single-update-propagates-everywhere workflow and reduces duplication across projects.

Dependencies:
- None. This is an external request to the `wl` team.

Deliverables:
- This work item serves as the feature request for the `wl` team.
- Ensure the parent epic SA-0MLRONXRF1N732R1 lists this item as a blocking dependency.

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).

- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

# Log projection helper: recentDispatchedItems

**Parent:** WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2 (Recent dispatches summary)

## Goal

Add a projection function to `downtime-log.ts` that reads the rolling dispatch log via the existing fail-safe reader and returns the up-to-20 most recent dispatched work items, deduplicated by id and ordered newest-first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New exported function `recentDispatchedItems(cwd, limit?)` reads via the existing fail-safe `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)`; a missing/unreadable/empty/malformed log yields `[]` with no throw.
- Non-dispatch-marker entries (pane-close/lifecycle entries with `entryType: 'pane-close'`) are ignored by the projection.
- Rows are deduplicated by work item id — one row per id — using that item's most recent log entry for ordering and metadata.
- Rows are ordered by their most recent log-entry timestamp, newest first.
- The result is capped at 20 rows (configurable via `limit`, default 20).
- Each row is a `RecentDispatchRow` carrying at least: `itemId`, `title`, `kind`, `latestOutcome` (when a pane-close entry exists), and `latestTimestamp`.
- A missing/empty title falls back to a placeholder (e.g. `[unknown]`) rather than a blank row; malformed JSONL lines are skipped without throwing.
- Unit tests cover: dedup by id, newest-first ordering, 20-row cap, kind/outcome mapping, missing title, malformed lines, and the empty/missing-log fail-safe path.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Define exported interface `RecentDispatchRow` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`.
2. Implement `recentDispatchedItems(cwd, limit = 20)` reading entries and reducing into a `Map<itemId, RecentDispatchRow>` keyed by id (last-write-wins on the newest entry).
3. Sort by latest timestamp descending, slice to `limit`.
4. Add unit tests to `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` (test-first: write the projection tests before the helper body).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None.

# Dispatches filter axis in the worklist

**Parent:** WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2 (Recent dispatches summary)

## Goal

Add a `dispatches` filter axis to `WorkItemListState` bound to the `/wl dispatches` internal command, honouring the existing single-filter-slot replace semantics and rendering a `(filtered: dispatches)` header label.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pressing `f` then `d` in the Herdr worklist activates a **recent dispatches** filter view. It follows the existing single filter-slot replace semantics: activating it clears any active stage/priority filter, and activating a stage/priority filter (or `f s s` / `f p s` / bare `/wl`) clears it. The list header renders a dispatches filter label (e.g. `(filtered: dispatches)`).
- `WorkItemListState` gains an `activeDispatchFilter` boolean (or equivalent) and an `applyDispatchFilter()` method; `clearFilter()` clears all three axes (stage, priority, dispatches).
- `dispatchChordCommand('/wl dispatches', state)` is recognised and handled internally (returns `true`, no pane/stdout routing); unknown values remain unhandled.
- `fetchItemsForView()` branches to the log-derived dispatches list when the dispatch filter is active, without changing the default browse list or the existing stage/priority fetch paths.
- The dispatches view is read-only and derived from the log only: it does not mutate the log or work items, does not change the default browse list or the existing stage/priority filters, and yields a header showing `N item(s)` for the number actually found (≤ 20).
- The dispatches view lists up to the 20 most recently dispatched work items, newest first, deduplicated by work item id, sourced from `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- Tests cover activation, replace/clear semantics across all three axes, the header label and item count, and chord recognition for `f d` → `/wl dispatches`.

## Problem statement

The worklist test suite is a 7,073-line monolith that covers all worklist
functionality — state, formatting, mouse input, key handling, rendering, TUI
integration, hydration, etc. Navigating and editing one concern requires holding
thousands of unrelated tests in view.

## Goal

Break the test file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No file exceeds 1,000 lines.
2. All imports still resolve; all existing tests pass without modification to
   their assertions (move-only refactor).
3. No new circular imports.
4. All related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate test groups and update imports; do not change test
  assertions or test logic.
- **Test-file scope.** This item exists because the producer declined to include
  test-file decomposition in WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B (intake Q1 → answer A):

# Remove dead top-level `singleFork` key in vitest.config.ts

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 — Reduce time to run tests

## Problem statement

`vitest.config.ts` sets `singleFork: true` at the top level of the `test`
block. Vitest 4 has no such top-level option — `singleFork` is a
`poolOptions.forks.*` key — so the setting is silently ignored (no warning is
emitted). The comment directly above it, "Force per-file isolation by limiting
to 1 active worker per file sequence", describes behaviour that is actually
provided by `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` (+ `pool: 'forks'`).

The dead key is harmless today, but it is misleading: a future reader may
believe the suite is serialised, and a migration to an option shape that *is*
read (or vitest version churn that starts warning) could confuse diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `singleFork: true` is removed from `vitest.config.ts`.
- The comment above it is rewritten (or removed) to state what actually
  enforces per-file isolation (`pool: 'forks'`, `isolate: true`,
  `maxWorkers: 4`), and that parallelism is otherwise intentional.
- Full canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) stays green with the same
  test counts; no runtime regression in either wall-clock or aggregate test
  time on the same host.

## Out of scope

Bumping `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` — that is the follow-up "Test-suite
parallelism: reconsider maxWorkers on hosts with more cores".

## Summary

Discovered during a `/skill:machine-hygiene` session (approval-gate output).
`scripts/evaluate.py` renders the Proposed actions table more than once in the
same run, and the three `renice` actions (node, pi, npm-exec-tsx) are each
proposed as separate numbered actions (observed as 2-4 duplicated by 5-7).

Impact: the operator sees 8 actions where there are 5 distinct remediations,
polluting the approval gate. The duplicate rows are also indistinguishable, so
approving "1" while declining "5" leaves the same target both executed and
skipped.

Fix: dedupe keep-first on `(action, target pids | scope)` and render the gate
findings exactly once per run.

Source: `discovered-from:machine-hygiene-session-2025-10-21`.

## Verified root cause (plan session)

Reproduced against `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/` in the SorraAgents repo
(the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` is byte-identical).

**A. Duplicate actions — `pressure_analysis.py`.**

- `analyze_pressures()` computes the top-3 RSS contributors **once**, then
  assigns the *same list object* to every elevated pressure
  (`pressure["contributors"] = contributors`).
- `propose_remediations()` loops pressures x contributors, emitting one
  `renice` per (pressure, contributor) for `memory_usage`, `memory_pressure`
  and `swap_usage`. Two elevated memory metrics x three contributors yields six
  `renice` actions for three distinct targets.
- `rank_actions()` only sorts by impact/risk ratio; it never dedupes, and
  `evaluate.py` never calls it.

Deterministic repro (synthetic metrics: `memory_usage` critical, `swap_usage`
warning, 3 RSS contributors): 6 actions, 3 distinct `(action, target)` pairs;
rows 1-3 are field-for-field identical to rows 4-6.

**B. Repeated rendering — `evaluate.py` / `tables.py`.**

- `render_approval_gate()` renders the Proposed actions table (copy 1).
- `prompt_for_approval()` renders it **again** before the prompt (copy 2).
- `render_human()` renders it a **third** time, together with a second copy of
  the before table and of the pressure analysis.

Measured on the interactive path: `## Proposed actions` appears 3 times and
`## Before` appears 2 times. On the `--yes` path the gate is skipped, so each
appears once. The work item's "twice" is therefore an undercount of the
interactive path, which is the observed run.

## Scope

In scope: dedupe proposals keep-first; render gate findings once per run.

Out of scope (recorded in Observations, not fixed here): `renice` safety checks
(current nice value, live test suites), ranking being unused by `evaluate.py`,
`--json` + interactive gating mixing prose and JSON, `TOP_CONTRIBUTORS` not
being configurable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `propose_remediations()` emits no two actions sharing a dedupe key
   of `(action, frozenset(target pids), target scope)`. A fixture with two
   elevated memory metrics (`memory_usage` + `swap_usage`) and three RSS
   contributors yields exactly 3 `renice` actions, not 6.
- **AC2** — Dedupe is keep-first: the surviving action is field-for-field
   identical to the first emitted duplicate (`action`, `target`, `reason`,
   `expected_impact`, `impact`, `risk`), so the relative order of distinct
   actions is unchanged.
- **AC3** — `rank_actions()` dedupes as well, so
   `rank_actions(propose_remediations(...))` and any caller passing a list that
   contains duplicates both return no duplicates ("dedupe before ranking").
- **AC4** — An interactive run prints the `## Proposed actions` table exactly
   once and the `## Before` table exactly once across the entire run (gate
   output plus final report), asserted with injected `input_fn`/`output_fn` and
   no real TTY.
- **AC5** — The `--yes` (auto-approve) path still prints both tables exactly
   once, and `--dry-run` and `--json` output shapes are unchanged.
- **AC6** — Approval stays row-accurate: approving row `n` of the displayed
   table approves that row, and `approved_count + declined_count` equals the
   number of displayed rows (no duplicate counted twice).

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py` — add `dedupe_actions()`
  and apply it in `propose_remediations()` and `rank_actions()`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/tables.py` — `prompt_for_approval()` gains
  `show_actions: bool = True` so a caller that already rendered the table can
  suppress the repeat; `render_approval_gate()` unchanged.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/evaluate.py` — record in the workflow result
  whether findings were already rendered; `render_human()` skips
  already-rendered findings; pass `show_actions=False` to the gate prompt.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_pressure_analysis.py` — dedupe unit tests.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_approval_gate.py` — single-render and
  row-accuracy tests.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_integration.py` — end-to-end section-count
  assertions for the interactive and `--yes` paths.

All paths are relative to the **SorraAgents** checkout
(`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents`, branch `dev`). The installed copy under
`~/.pi/agent/skills/` is a build artefact refreshed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`
and must not be edited directly.

## Minimal implementation (test-first)

1. Add the failing tests first: duplicate-`renice` fixture (AC1/AC2),
   `rank_actions` dedupe (AC3), section counts for both paths (AC4/AC5),
   row accuracy (AC6).
2. `pressure_analysis.py`: `dedupe_actions(actions)` keyed on
   `(action, frozenset(pids | []), target.get("scope"))`, keeping the first
   occurrence; call it at the end of `propose_remediations()` and at the start
   of `rank_actions()`.
3. `tables.py`: add the `show_actions` parameter to `prompt_for_approval()`
   (default `True` preserves current behaviour and keeps existing tests green).
4. `evaluate.py`: add `findings_rendered` to the `run_workflow()` result (`True`
   when the gate printed findings); `render_human()` gains
   `include_findings: bool | None = None` defaulting to
   `not result.get("findings_rendered", False)`; pass `show_actions=False` in
   the gate's prompt call.
5. Docs: no `SKILL.md` change needed (internal behaviour); the skill tests are
   the contract.
6. Run the changed-scope test gate for the skill tests, then the dev-push full
   suite gate.

## Observations (not in scope — recorded, not fixed here)

- `renice` is proposed without inspecting the target's current nice value; the
  observed run targeted two live test suites already at nice 19/0. Tracked
  separately as a discovered item (see Appendix Q2).
- `evaluate.py` never calls `rank_actions()`, so actions are displayed in
  emission order rather than impact/risk order.
- `--json` without `--yes` still runs the interactive gate, mixing prose and
  JSON on stdout.
- `TOP_CONTRIBUTORS` is a module constant rather than a `config.yaml` tunable.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 (plan): effort/risk pre-check returned `skip` (Extra Small / Low).
  Ran the six automated review stages against the existing content; rewrote the
  description with a verified root cause, six testable ACs, `Key Files` and a
  test-first implementation sketch. No children created (single vertical
  slice); AC coverage review returned `proceed`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where does the fix land: the installed skill at
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` or the SorraAgents repo?**
  Answer (plan, evidence-based): the SorraAgents repo,
  `skill/machine-hygiene/`, on branch `dev`. Evidence: `diff` shows all three
  scripts byte-identical between repo and installed copy, and prior
  machine-hygiene work shipped from `skill/machine-hygiene/`
  (`WL-0MULOZ46M003THM1`, `WL-0MULP55W1009G62B`). Source: repo inspection,
  this session.
- **Q2 — Is the producer's secondary finding (renice without a nice-value
  check, targeting live test suites) part of this item?**
  Answer (plan assumption, pending producer confirmation): **no** — dedupe and
  single-render are the stated fix; the safety check is a separate behavioural
  change tracked as its own discovered item. **Recommended:** keep it separate
  — the dedupe fix is independently correct and testable, and merging widens an
  Extra Small chore into a semantics change requiring process-nice inspection.
  Evidence: the producer comment on this item labels it "Secondary finding",
  while the Summary/Fix line covers duplication only. Source: `@producer`
  comment 2026-10-21, this session's repro.
  **OPEN QUESTION** for `@producer`: if the nice-value guard must ship here
  instead, reply and the two items will be merged. Not blocking — the duplication
  fix stands on its own.

   `DisplayRow`, `DisplayHeadingRow`, `ChordState`, `ParsedMouseEvent`,
   `MouseDragState`, `MouseClickState`, `MouseAction`. **Internal** (declared in
   the new modules, exported from them for sibling use, but *not* re-exported by

   `HelpIconRow`, `NoteEditAction`, `ReviewQueueBannerState`, `PodcastNotice`,
   `ExecuteResult`, `PodcastTargetResolution`, `ViewMode`, `MIN_META_SHARE`,
   `MAX_META_SHARE`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*
4. `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` is green: every baseline/consumer symbol still

5. `tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) succeeds and the full

6. Documentation that names these symbols is updated to the new module paths:

   `ANSI`/colour references), `docs/COLOUR-MAPPING.md` (line 77) if the
   `formatItemLine` reference needs the new home (deferred there if format has
   not moved yet — record the deferral in a comment).

   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners such as

# Split worklist TUI loop into context and handlers

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 6 of 7 (the hard part).

## Target outcome

`runWorklistTui` (currently lines 5581–7899, ~2,319 lines of nested closures over
one mutable context) becomes a thin orchestrator over named handler modules,
with a **single interface-typed context object owned by one module** and passed
explicitly to handler functions — no state duplication and no class-based
controller rewrite (parent constraint).

## Scope (measured closure groups inside `runWorklistTui`)

| New module | Contents | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.tui-context.ts` | The context interface + factory: `opts`, `termSize`, `items`, `state`, `renderer`, `inputActive`, view flags (`formState`, `preFormMode`, `preHelpMode`, `helpScrollOffset`, `shipItDialog`, `podcastNotice`, `blockedNotice`), freeze/sprint flags, dispose hooks. Single owner of the mutable context (AC5) | ~250 |
| `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` | Pane gate, agent tracker, live event subscriptions, pane-marker apply/refresh/batching, metadata blocker resolution + cache (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8), freeze-state refresh, review-queue sprint state | ~560 |
| `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` | Non-blocking sync status notice (F3 — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N), `cleanup`, `closeEventSubscriber`, `doRefresh` (single-flight + pending), `doSync`, `openShipItDialog` / `openShipItDialogGuarded` | ~480 |
| `worklist.tui-input.ts` | `dispatchMouse`, `handleKeyInput`, streaming stdin decode (`onData` + `KeypressDecoder`), `readKeyFile`/`writeKeyFile`, `buildHelpEntries`/`buildHelpIconLegend` | ~800 |
| `worklist.tui-render.ts` | `render`, `onResize`, `TaskScheduler` wiring, hydrator runner, resume poll, db-change watch, and the `runWorklistTui` orchestrator that constructs the context and registers handlers | ~570 |

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `runWorklistTui` is retained at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical
   signature and return type (`Promise<WorkItem | undefined>`), implemented as a
   thin orchestrator (context construction + handler registration + teardown);
   no module and no single exported function carries the former 2,319-line body
   (AC1).
2. Every new module ≤1,000 lines with a responsibility doc comment; the TUI-local
   sub-banners (metadata-panel dependency blockers — WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8,
   review-queue depth indicator, event-driven window status — WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ,
   non-blocking sync status notice — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N, mouse event dispatch —
   WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ AC2–AC6, streaming stdin decode — WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH,
   consolidated scheduler loop — WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP, hydrator —
   WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI) and their inline work-item ids move verbatim (AC6).
3. **Single context, explicit passing.** The context type is declared once in
   `worklist.tui-context.ts`; handler modules receive it as a parameter and
   never re-declare a mutable field it already owns. `WorkItemListState`
   remains a single instance created by the orchestrator (AC5); the split guard's
   single-owner gate stays green.
4. Lifecycle ordering is preserved exactly: event-subscription setup, pane gate,
   refresh single-flight/pending, scheduler ticks, hydrator, resume poll and
   teardown order are unchanged — verified by the unmodified
   `worklist-integration.test.ts`, `worklist-active-pane-marker.test.ts`,
   `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts`, `worklist-consolidated-refresh.test.ts`,
   `worklist-watch.test.ts`, `worklist-inflight.test.ts`,
   `worklist-sync-notice.test.ts` and `worklist.test.ts` TUI blocks (AC3).
5. Split guard, `tsc --noEmit`/build and the full `packages/herdr` suite pass;
   no new cycle; no runtime barrel import (AC4, AC9).
6. Docs updated: `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block, `onPaneFocused`
   and `isInputActive` references at ~1619 and ~1781, and the ~1829 "task
   registration in `worklist.ts`" note), `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`,
   `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — all path references resolve
   to the new modules.
7. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
   → Owned by this slice: `WorkItemListState` and the extracted TUI context each live in exactly one module and no mutable state is duplicated.

## Minimal implementation

1. Introduce `worklist.tui-context.ts` with the context interface and factory;
   move the `opts`/state/flag declarations into it **without** changing any
   initial value or ordering.
2. Extract `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` (subscriptions, pane markers, blockers,
   freeze/sprint state) as functions taking the context.
3. Extract `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` (`doRefresh`/`doSync`/ship-it dialog/notice/
   cleanup) as functions taking the context.
4. Extract `worklist.tui-input.ts` (`handleKeyInput`/`dispatchMouse`/`onData`/
   key-file IO/help entries) as functions taking the context.
5. Extract `worklist.tui-render.ts` (render/resize/scheduler/hydrator/resume
   poll/db-change watch) and reduce `runWorklistTui` to orchestration.
   Land steps 1–5 as **separate commits**, each with the full suite green, so a
   behavioural regression is attributable to one closure group.
6. Run guard + build + suite; update docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts` — new (single context owner).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-handlers.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-refresh.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-input.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-render.ts` — new (holds the orchestrator).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — re-exports `runWorklistTui`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — consumer; must compile unchanged.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md` and the five `docs/dev/*` files listed above.

## Constraints

- No class-based controller conversion, no state duplication, no reordering of
  lifecycle steps, no changed defaults or timings.
- The context is interface-typed and passed explicitly; closures may become
  module functions but must not change observable behaviour.
- No barrel/`index.ts` imports inside the new modules; no test edits.

## Dependencies

- `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J` — refactor guard (test-first).
- `WL-0MVND6DHH008R3LG` — constants/types/layout.
- `WL-0MVND6F9V004IQ3V` — state/navigation.
- `WL-0MVND6H5Q006YO9Z` — presentation.
- `WL-0MVND6J090041GWK` — input pipeline (key/mouse handlers move with it).
- `WL-0MVND6KVF0089878` — renderer/commands (the loop dispatches through them).

## Deliverables

Five TUI modules with a thin `runWorklistTui`, guard + full suite green, docs
updated.

Discovered during plan review of WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (discovered-from:WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ).

Producer finding from the machine-hygiene session (2025-10-21): propose_remediations() in skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py emits a renice action for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In the observed run every proposed target was already at nice 19 or 0, and the targets included two live test suites (AI_Hell vitest, tce-the-rising browser suite) - the action would have slowed active work.

Suggested fix (from producer): skip renice when min(nice) over the target pids is already >= the proposed nice value, and surface the current nice value in the action's reason/target so the operator can see why an action is proposed or suppressed.

Note: this is deliberately separate from the duplication fix in WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (dedupe + single render); this item is the semantic safety change and needs process-nice collection support.

Scope: scanning niceness (/proc/<pid>/stat field 19) for target pids, suppressing no-op renicces, and tests for both suppressed and emitted cases. Related: skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py (propose_remediations), metrics collection if nice must be collected centrally.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions

- Q: Should a suppressed renice be surfaced as a visible record (e.g. a skipped/informational entry showing current nice, per the producer's "see why an action is proposed or suppressed"), or is a silent drop from the actions list acceptable?
  - Answer (producer, 2025-11-15, on WL-0MVNR3ZV30098BI6): "silent is OK". Final: **silent drop** — suppressed renicces are not added to the actions list; no informational entry required.
  - Impact: child WL-0MWH746JX0073R7F AC2 stands as written ("not added to the actions list"); no extra test case needed for suppressed-visibility. AC3 (surface current nice on *emitted* renice) is unchanged.
  - Context: the producer's suggested fix wording covered both proposed and suppressed, but the child AC2 already drops suppressed actions entirely, so no change is needed.
- Q (open — implementer default): How should `get_nice_value()` returning `None` (unreadable `/proc/<pid>/stat`) be handled in the "min over target PIDs" computation? Answer: OPEN — default expectation is unreadable PIDs are excluded from the min, and a fully-unreadable target treats as not-suppressed (propose as today); implementer to confirm during implementation. Context: recorded in WL-0MWH746JX0073R7F Open Questions.

# Extract search, sync and import-export modules and close out

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGHNR0019OLT — decompose `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
_(parent retired and deleted; this item was promoted to top-level on
2026-11-19 by `wl doctor --fix` — see comment WL-C0MWNOXRYQ004KSCR)_
**Type:** task (move-only extraction + closeout)
**Position in chain:** 7 of 7 — final verification and docs.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the remaining concerns (FTS/semantic search, Git/JSONL
sync, JSONL import/export) out of the god class, the public API proven
byte-compatible, the docs re-pointed, and the 1,000-line ceiling verified by
machine and by hand — leaving `database.ts` as a thin façade.

## Context

Remaining concerns of the god class, ~790 combined lines:

- `database/search.ts` — `search`, `rebuildFtsIndex`, semantic-index
  create/trigger/remove (~210 lines). `docs/dev/fts.md` names
  `WorklogDatabase.search()`.
- `database/sync.ts` — `refreshFromGit`, `exportForSync`, export timestamps,
  `countDirtyRecords`, delta metadata, `deleteLocalJsonl`,
  `refreshFromJsonlIfNewer`, auto-sync triggers (~380 lines).
  `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` names `exportForSync()`.
- `database/import-export.ts` — `import`, `upsertItems`, `clear`,
  `getAll*` snapshots (~200 lines).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `packages/shared/src/database/search.ts`, `sync.ts` and `import-export.ts`
   exist; the methods listed in Context live in exactly one of them as pure
   functions over the shared context, and `database.ts` keeps only thin
   delegating members with identical signatures.
2. **Ceiling met.** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and every file under
   `packages/shared/src/database/` is ≤ 1,000 lines (target: largest extracted
   module ≤ 700). Verified with `wc -l` output recorded in the work item; the
   guard suite's `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is emptied and stays empty.
3. **Public API unchanged.** `WorklogDatabase` (all public method signatures and
   constructor), plus `WorklogDatabaseServices`, `JsonlImportResult`,
   `GitTarget`, `UpdateIfMatchesResult` and `normalizeTitleForMatch` remain
   importable from the unchanged specifier `@worklog/shared` (entry
   `dist/database.js`). No changes to `src/**` or `packages/herdr/src/**`
   consumer code. The slice-1 guard exports baseline is still fully matched.
4. **Move-only, behaviour-preserving.** No logic, SQL, error-message, ordering,
   or schema changes; existing test assertions are unmodified and the suite is
   green. Test files may be split/moved only where a test file itself exceeds
   1,000 lines (lockstep rule), with import paths the only mechanical change —
   this child performs both splits: `tests/database.test.ts` (3,780 lines on
   `dev` at planning, 2026-11-19) and `tests/next-regression.test.ts` (2,323
   lines) each become files of ≤ 1,000
   lines with `describe` titles, assertions and fixtures unchanged.
5. **No circular imports.** The extracted-module import graph is acyclic; no
   module imports the `database.ts` façade. Shared types live in a context
   module that every extracted module may import — asserted by the slice-1
   guard test.
6. **Responsibilities documented.** `packages/shared/README.md` (Package
   Structure) and each new module's header comment state its single
   responsibility and its boundary.
7. **No performance regression** in the `wl next` path: final `npm run
   benchmark:wl-next:json` comparison against the child-1 baseline within
   run-to-run noise (the extraction moves code only, and
   `EdgeCache`/effective-priority caching semantics are unchanged).
8. **Builds and tests.** `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build` and the full
   project test suite all pass.
9. **Documentation updated.** All related documentation reflects the changes,
   including code comments, `packages/shared/README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`,
   `docs/dev/fts.md`, `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md` and
   `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (each currently names
   `packages/shared/src/database.ts` as the home of a concern). The final
   `wc -l` evidence and benchmark output are recorded in comments on this item.

## Minimal implementation

1. Move `search.ts`, `sync.ts`, `import-export.ts`; rewire `database.ts` to
   delegate; keep every SQL string, export predicate and watermark byte-identical.
2. Split `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/next-regression.test.ts`
   mechanically along existing `describe` boundaries (≤ 1,000 lines per file;
   imports only, no assertion edits).
3. Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` in the guard suite (one line).
4. Update `packages/shared/README.md` (Package Structure) and the four docs;
   sweep `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` references too.
5. Run `npm run build:shared`, `npm run build`, `npm run benchmark:wl-next:json`
   and `/skill:test` (full scope, per the test skill — this is the closeout
   gate); record all outputs.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/shared/src/database/search.ts` — new
- `packages/shared/src/database/sync.ts` — new
- `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts` — new
- `packages/shared/src/database/context.ts` — shared types/context every
  extracted module imports (`GitTarget`, `JsonlImportResult`,
  `WorklogDatabaseServices`, sync state, semantic-search handle)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — final façade (~400 lines)
- `packages/shared/README.md` — Package Structure section
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/dev/fts.md`,
  `docs/dependency-reconciliation.md`, `docs/design/incremental-sync.md`,
  `docs/validation/status-stage-inventory.md` — file references
- `tests/database.test.ts`, `tests/next-regression.test.ts` → split into
  ≤ 1,000-line files each
- `packages/shared/src/database/decomposition-guard.test.ts` — allowlist
  emptied
- `bench/wl-next-perf.ts` — read-only (invoked, not changed)

## Dependencies

Blocked by children 2–6 (all extraction slices) — the last slice.

**Current blocker state (verified 2026-11-19):** slices 1–6 have landed on
`dev`; the only tracked outbound dependency, WL-0MVOBP6K0007574C (dependency
and comment modules), is `deleted` with its work merged
(`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`, `comments.ts` and
`tests/database-dependencies-comments-extraction.test.ts` are present). No
open blockers remain — this item is dispatchable.

## Constraints

- Move-only until all six slices are green; the closeout child may perform only
  the mechanical splits, docs re-pointing and the verification gates above.
- Serialise with WL-0MVGKGJXJ000ISBU (`persistent-store.ts`) — that item is
  now `deleted`, so the serialisation constraint is satisfied and no longer
  holds this item back.

## Plan review — 2026-11-19 (auto-complete, no decomposition)

**Decision: no further decomposition.** This is a single bounded, atomic
move-only slice — the three extractions, the two mechanical test splits, the
`SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` emptying and the closeout gates must land together (the guard
test fails if the allowlist is emptied before the façade is under the ceiling),
so child items would break the atomicity they depend on. The description
already carries 9 measurable ACs and a 5-step minimal implementation, which is
sufficient for direct implementation.

`dev` state measured at planning time:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `packages/shared/src/database.ts` | 2,178 |
| `tests/database.test.ts` | 3,780 |
| `tests/next-regression.test.ts` | 2,323 |

- `packages/shared/src/database/` on `dev` holds `audit`, `comments`,
  `context`, `critical-escalation`, `dependencies`, `hierarchy`,
  `next-pipeline`, `priority`, `sort`, `work-items` (plus the guard test);
  `search.ts`, `sync.ts` and `import-export.ts` do **not** exist yet.
- `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is currently `['database.ts']` (guard test line 89).
- Blockers: none (see Dependencies). Plan-approval gate: **not required**
  (effort `L`, risk `Medium`).

Six review stages, run against the existing content:

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — all 9 ACs trace back to the Goal/Context;
   no invented or contradictory ACs. Stale test line counts in AC4 corrected.
2. **Completeness** — description, ACs and Key Files complete; `Key Files`
   passes `validate_key_files_format` (0 issues). Added the shared context
   module that AC5 implies but Key Files omitted.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — the only outbound dependency is satisfied
   (merged, item `deleted`); no test-first child needed because the existing
   suite is the verification and the test splits are lockstep with the move.
4. **Scope sizing** — one deliverable increment; no split (see Decision).
5. **Acceptance & testability** — every AC has a pass/fail check (`wc -l`,
   guard suite, `npm run build:shared` / `npm run build`,
   `npm run benchmark:wl-next:json`, `/skill:test` full scope, doc greps).
6. **Polish & handoff** — retired parent, retired serialisation item and
   blocker state made explicit; resume note below.

**Resume note for the next implement session.** An earlier implement run left
work in `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOBP8MC0093Y7T-extract-search-sync-and-import-export-mo`
(branch `wl-WL-0MVOBP8MC0093Y7T-…`, HEAD `46790907c`), part of it uncommitted;
both prior runs aborted in the test-fix loop. Measured there: façade
`database.ts` **910** lines, largest module **669** (`next-pipeline.ts`),
`search.ts` 270 / `sync.ts` 433 / `import-export.ts` 339, `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST`
already `[]`, and every split test file ≤ 1,000 lines (largest 884). Resume and
finish that work — re-run the gates and commit — rather than re-doing the
extraction from scratch.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-19 — `/skill:plan`: pre-check `decision: plan` (L/Medium); Process
  step 1 auto-complete (single atomic slice, measurable ACs present); six
  review stages run; description corrected (retired parent, current `dev` line
  counts, `context.ts` added to Key Files, blocker/serialisation state);
  AC-coverage review `proceed` (leaf item, no children); stage →
  `plan_complete`.

## Impact

Maintainers can now change search, sync or JSONL import/export by editing one focused module instead of a 2,000-line file, with the public `WorklogDatabase` API and behaviour unchanged for every caller.

# Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble shared by gitPushDataFileToBranch and rewriteAndForcePushDataFile

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 (*Extract sync worktree, remote-fetch and push modules*, sync split, child 5 of 6) — filed under that item's constraint that known awkwardness in this region is recorded as a work item rather than refactored inline.

## Problem statement

`src/sync/push.ts` contains two public push paths — `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental commit on the existing data-ref history) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (fresh orphan commit force-pushed over a polluted history) — and each carries its own near-identical copy of the same preamble: cross-project guard, `refs/heads/`/`refs/tags/` safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, repo-root/relative-path resolution, data-file existence check, `withTempWorktree(...)`, and the force-add / `diff --cached` / commit staging dance. A fix to any one of those steps (a guard message, a path-handling bug, an empty-stage policy) must currently be made twice and can silently drift.

## Users

- **Maintainer of the sync layer** — "As a maintainer, I want the shared preamble in one private helper so a guard or path-handling fix applies to both push paths, and each public function reads as its actual difference (empty-stage policy + push mode)."
- **Reviewer of a sync change** — "As a reviewer, I want to see one copy of each guard so I can verify a safety change without diffing two near-identical blocks."
- **Operator running `wl sync` / `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push`** — indirect: both paths keep their current observable behaviour (silent no-op vs hard failure) exactly.

## Existing state

- `gitPushDataFileToBranch(repoDataFilePath, commitMessage, target): Promise<void>` — shared steps, then cleans foreign tracked files from the data branch, copies the JSONL, `add -f`, `diff --cached`, **silently returns** when nothing is staged, commits, then `git push --no-verify <remote> HEAD:<ref>`.
- `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile(repoDataFilePath, commitMessage, target): Promise<string>` — same shared steps (minus the foreign-file cleanup), **throws `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref`** when nothing is staged, commits, then `git push --force --no-verify`, then reads `rev-parse HEAD` inside the worktree callback (the returned `tipSha`), updates the local remote-tracking ref, and returns the SHA.
- Differences that must survive the refactor: (a) empty-stage policy `silent return` vs `throw`; (b) existence check `silent return` vs `throw Worklog data file not found: …`; (c) safety-guard message — the incremental path appends the hint `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 to bypass the pre-push hook.`, the rewrite path does not; (d) `withTempWorktree` option `forceOrphan: true` only on the rewrite path; (e) push flags `--no-verify` vs `--force --no-verify`; (f) only the rewrite path returns a value (the new tip SHA) and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` afterwards.
- Current sizes: `src/sync/push.ts` 199 lines, `src/sync.ts` (barrel) 100 lines — both far below the 1,000-line ceiling; this item is about removing duplication, not about the ceiling.
- Structural gate already in place: `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` parses the module tree and asserts the frozen barrel surface (`tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json`, 34 symbols), the ≤ 1,000-line ceiling and an acyclic import graph. A private helper inside `push.ts` changes none of those, so this gate must stay green **without** re-baselining.
- Test coverage today: `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` covers orphan-branch creation, target validation and the `--no-verify` source grep; `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` covers the happy-path rewrite, the refs safety rejection, the missing-file throw and sequential reentrancy. **Not covered:** the incremental path's silent no-op on an empty stage, and the rewrite path's `Nothing staged for the rewrite` throw — i.e. exactly the two policies that distinguish the paths and are most at risk in a dedupe refactor.

## Desired change

Introduce one private helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) that owns the shared preamble and delegates the mode-specific tail to a callback:

- Guard + resolve: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo(repoDataFilePath)`, the `refs/heads/`/`refs/tags/` rejection, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` / `path.resolve()` and the existence check.
- Materialise: `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, ..., { forceOrphan })`, `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- Empty-stage policy as an explicit option (`'skip' | 'throw'`) — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op without invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing message.
- Commit, then invoke the caller's `run` with the worktree context (`worktreePath`, `relativePath`, escaped forms) so each caller performs only its own push (`--no-verify` vs `--force --no-verify`) and, for the rewrite path, reads `rev-parse HEAD`.
- The safety-guard workaround hint is a parameter so both messages stay byte-identical to today.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper → do their mode-specific push (and, for rewrite, update the tracking ref + return the SHA).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
2. **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
3. **Existing suites pass and the grep assertion is not weakened.** `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` and `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` pass unchanged in intent; if the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion still exists it is re-pointed (and still asserts the same property) rather than deleted or loosened — if WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z has already replaced it with a behavioural test, no re-point is needed and this clause is satisfied trivially.
4. **Size and structural gate.** `src/sync/push.ts` shrinks (net fewer lines); no file exceeds 1,000 lines; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` is green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` **unchanged** (no re-baselining); `npm run build` is green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.
5. **No surface change.** The `src/sync.ts` barrel exports are identical (same names, same signatures — asserted by `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`); no consumer edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.
6. **Testing / validation criterion.** The two currently-uncovered policies in AC2(c) and AC2(d) each gain at least one meaningful test that fails if the policy is swapped between the two paths (negative proof, not just a happy-path assertion).
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the `src/sync/push.ts` module header (naming the helper and the two policies) and the `src/sync/push.ts` row/table entry in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if its description changes. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature, no behavioural, no error-message change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` surface is unchanged.
- Helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts` — `src/sync/worktree.ts` remains a generic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts` (see Risks).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only; the full suite is enforced at the dev-push gate.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy parameter applied to both paths would silently turn the rewrite path's hard failure into a no-op (publishing nothing while reporting success) or turn a routine no-change sync into an error. Mitigation: AC2(c)/AC6 tests pin both directions.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two safety-guard messages would drop the `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where it does not belong). Mitigation: hint is an explicit parameter; AC2(a) asserts the exact text.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }` through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path would fetch the polluted ref again (the exact bug the split fixed). Mitigation: `rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` rewrites a seeded polluted remote and asserts foreign items are gone.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing; the helper's generic return (`Promise<T | undefined>`) must stay honest so callers cannot silently drop the SHA. Mitigation: rewrite path throws on `undefined` or types the helper with a non-optional return for the `'throw'` policy.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The read paths in `src/sync/remote.ts` repeat the same `assertDataFileInCwdRepo` + `git rev-parse --git-dir` + repo-root resolution trio. That is a separate opportunity: record it as a linked follow-up work item, do not absorb it here.
- **Assumption:** the helper lives in `push.ts` rather than `worktree.ts` (see Appendix Q1); **assumption:** the empty-stage policy remains path-specific rather than unified (Q2); **assumption:** the source-grep assertion is left to WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z if that lands first (Q3).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/sync/push.ts` — Needs the new private `withDataFileInTempWorktree` helper; both public functions rewritten on top of it; module header updated.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only (unchanged): supplies `withTempWorktree`, `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only (unchanged): supplies `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRelativePath`.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `getRemoteTrackingRef` used by the rewrite path's post-push bookkeeping.
- `src/sync.ts` — Unchanged barrel; verify exports are byte-identical.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — Add the incremental-path policy tests (silent no-op on empty stage, silent no-op on missing file); re-point the `--no-verify` grep if it still exists.
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — Add the empty-stage `Nothing staged for the rewrite` test; keep the refs-rejection and missing-file tests.
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green): structural gates over the module tree; `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` must not be regenerated.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — Update the `src/sync/push.ts` row if the module's description (helper present) changes.

## Related work

Curated from repo/worklog search plus the `find-related` run for this item (its raw keyword report was reviewed but is transient; the items that matter are listed below and the rest were keyword noise):

- **WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1** — *Extract sync worktree, remote-fetch and push modules* (open, `plan_complete`, high). The split that created `src/sync/push.ts`; this item's outbound dependency and the source of the duplication.
- **WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z** — *Replace the source-grep push assertion in tests/sync-worktree.test.ts with a behavioural test* (open, low). Overlaps AC3: it removes the grep assertion this item would otherwise have to re-point.
- **WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ** — *Refactor: decompose src/sync.ts god class (goal: no file > 1000 lines)* (open). The parent epic of the sync decomposition.
- **WL-0MVP9SEJZ000KWXJ** — *Finalise sync barrel, documentation and close-out* (completed). Landed the barrel/`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` layout this item must keep in sync.
- **WL-0MSGNDSCR0096MCR** — *wl sync fails: duplicate 'git worktree add' in withTempWorktree* (completed). Prior bug in exactly this worktree path; the behaviour must not regress.
- **Potentially related docs:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (§ sync module map and "where to change what" table), `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (dev-facing orientation to the sync layout, including the worktree-isolation rules the helper must preserve), `docs/design/incremental-sync.md` (why the incremental path commits onto existing ref history instead of forcing).
- **Duplicate check:** performed (`wl search` over *push preamble / worktree helper / deduplicate preamble* keywords) — no overlapping or duplicate item found; this is the only item covering the push-preamble dedupe.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Answers below record the agent's research plus the recommended option that was applied pending producer override (per the interview contract, the recommendation is advisory and the operator may change it).

- **Q1 — Where should the shared helper live: private in `src/sync/push.ts`, or exported from `src/sync/worktree.ts`?**
  - **Recommended:** private in `src/sync/push.ts` — both consumers are in that module, and `worktree.ts` stays a generic lifecycle layer with no knowledge of data files.
  - **Answer (applied, producer may override):** private in `src/sync/push.ts`. Evidence: `grep -rn "gitPushDataFileToBranch|rewriteAndForcePushDataFile" src/` shows the only callers are `src/sync/push.ts` (definitions), the barrel, and three consumers that go through the barrel; `worktree.ts` is imported by `remote.ts` and `push.ts` and documents itself as data-file-agnostic. Source: repo inspection of `src/sync/push.ts`, `src/sync/worktree.ts`, `src/sync/remote.ts`.
- **Q2 — Should the empty-stage policy stay path-specific (`skip` for incremental, `throw` for rewrite) or be unified?**
  - **Recommended:** keep it path-specific and make it an explicit helper option — a silent no-op on the rewrite path would publish nothing while reporting success, and a throw on the incremental path would break routine no-change syncs.
  - **Answer (applied, producer may override):** path-specific, passed as an option. Evidence: `src/sync/push.ts:98-100` returns silently from inside the worktree callback, `src/sync/push.ts:177-179` throws `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref`; no test currently pins either behaviour, hence AC2(c) and AC6. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q3 — AC3 mentions "any source-grep assertion is re-pointed, not weakened", but WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z is dedicated to deleting that assertion. Which item owns it?**
  - **Recommended:** this item re-points only if the grep assertion is still present when it is implemented; otherwise the clause is satisfied trivially and WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z owns the removal.
  - **Answer (applied, producer may override):** conditional re-point, as recommended; no work is duplicated if the sibling lands first. Evidence: `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts:286-305` currently greps `src/sync/push.ts` for `git -C … push --no-verify`; the sibling item's AC1 replaces it with mock-trace assertions. Source: repo inspection plus `wl show WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z`.
- **Q4 — Does the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts` belong in this item's scope?**
  - **Recommended:** no — file it as a separate follow-up (recorded in Risks) so this item stays a pure, reviewable dedupe of the two push paths.
  - **Answer (applied, producer may override):** out of scope; noted as a scope-creep risk with a follow-up recommendation. Evidence: `src/sync/remote.ts:40,100` repeat `assertDataFileInCwdRepo` + `git rev-parse --git-dir` + `getRepoRoot/getRepoRelativePath` on the read paths. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q5 — This item's outbound dependency made it undispatchable. How should planning proceed?**
  - **Context:** `wl` derived status `blocked` for this item because its outbound dependency **WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1** (*Extract sync worktree, remote-fetch and push modules*) was still `open` at `plan_complete`, even though that extraction is fully landed on `dev` (commits `a0acda4f`, `fa729875`, `129bbaef`, `05c5330f`). The plan skill's claim guard (`StatusLifecycle.require_claimed`) fails closed outside `in_progress`, so no planning mutations could be made.
  - **Recommended:** advance the stale dependency first (its code is demonstrably landed), then plan normally — rather than bypassing the claim guard.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28):** run `/skill:implement WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1` and, once that skill marks it `completed`, proceed with planning. Evidence: dependency is now `completed`/`in_review` (commit `0a7d0b73` adds the `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` document its AC7 required); this item is unblocked and planning completed with 100% AC coverage.

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 (sync split, child 5 of 6).

## Problem

`tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` ("push command uses --no-verify to avoid recursive pre-push hook") reads production source and greps for the literal push command line. That is anti-pattern #1 in the shared Test Writing Guidelines (grep source instead of asserting behaviour): it couples the test to a file path and a literal command string, so any legitimate move (as in the sync split) or message reformat breaks it, while a real regression in push behaviour would not necessarily be caught.

Child 5 re-pointed the grep from `src/sync.ts` to `src/sync/push.ts` (assertions unchanged) to keep the gate green — a stop-gap, not a fix.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test to prove the observable behaviour — that pushes performed by the sync push paths bypass the pre-push hook — without grepping source text.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The test drives `gitPushDataFileToBranch` through the existing git mock (which already traces invocations) and asserts the recorded push invocation contains `--no-verify` (and, for the rewrite path, `--force --no-verify`).
2. No `readFileSync` of production source remains in the test for this behaviour.
3. The test fails if `--no-verify` is removed from either push command (negative proof), and passes on the current tree.
4. Only `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (plus mock assertions if required) changes; no production behaviour change; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.

## Notes

- Related: WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 re-pointed the assertion; this item removes the anti-pattern.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts`

# Pin push-path policy divergence with tests

Test-first safety net for WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push
preamble shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`*).

**No production code changes in this child.** It adds the tests that must be
green **before** `src/sync/push.ts` is refactored, so the dedupe is verified
against pinned behaviour instead of against a re-read of the same code.

## Why

The two push paths deliberately diverge on two policies, and **neither
divergent policy is covered by a test today**:

| Policy | `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) | `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (rewrite) |
|---|---|---|
| Empty stage (`diff --cached` names nothing) | returns silently | throws `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` |
| Data file missing | returns silently | throws `Worklog data file not found: …` |

Those are exactly the policies a shared helper can silently unify. Each needs a
**negative-proof** test: one that fails if the policy is swapped between the two
paths (an assertion that the other path's behaviour does *not* occur).

Two further divergences must also be pinned byte-exactly:

- the safety-guard message — the incremental path appends
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 to bypass the pre-push hook.`, the rewrite path
  does not;
- the push flags — `--no-verify` (incremental) vs `--force --no-verify`
  (rewrite).

## Scope — tests only

### `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (incremental path; mock-`git` driven today)

- **Empty stage** resolves without error and performs no push (no `push` call
  in the mock trace / no ref created on the fake remote).
- **Missing data file** (path inside the repo, file absent) resolves without
  error — i.e. it does **not** throw `Worklog data file not found`.
- **`refs/tags/*` rejection** asserts today's exact message text, including the
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint.
- **Cross-project guard** still fires when the data file lives in a different
  git repository than the process cwd.
- **Re-point the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion** (currently
  `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts:286-305`): it must keep asserting "no push line
  in `src/sync/push.ts` lacks `--no-verify`" and "a `push --no-verify` line
  exists". Re-pointed, **not deleted or loosened**. The sibling that would
  delete it (WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z) is still at `idea`, so this item owns the
  re-point.

### `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` (rewrite path; real-`git` driven)

- **Empty stage** rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite` — and does
  **not** resolve.
- **`refs/heads/*` rejection** asserts today's exact message text and asserts
  the message does **not** carry the `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH` hint.
- **`--force`** is used: the remote ref is replaced rather than fast-forwarded.
- Keep the existing missing-file, refs-rejection and reentrancy tests unchanged
  in intent.

## Implementation notes

- The mock git (`tests/cli/mock-bin/git`) has **no `diff` handler**: its
  fallback prints the argv to stdout, which makes `diff --cached` look
  non-empty and hides the empty-stage branch. For the incremental empty-stage
  test, prefer a **real-`git`** test in the style of
  `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — seed a bare remote whose
  `refs/worklog/data` already contains byte-identical JSONL, then call
  `gitPushDataFileToBranch` with the same bytes so the copy stages nothing. If
  the mock must gain a `diff` case instead, gate it behind an env var so
  existing suites are unaffected.
- The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup means a seeded ref should
  contain only the data file, or the cleanup will stage deletions.
- Do not weaken an existing assertion to make a new test pass; if a test cannot
  be expressed behaviourally, record an open question rather than grep source.

## Constraints

- No production-code edits (`src/**`).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - **Empty stage (negative proof)** — the incremental path resolves without error and performs no push; an added test fails if the incremental path starts throwing.
  - **Empty stage (negative proof)** — the rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref`; an added test fails if the rewrite path starts resolving.
  - **Missing data file (negative proof)** — the incremental path resolves (no throw) and the rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; each assertion fails if the policies are swapped.
  - **(a) Refs rejection** — `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` rejected on both paths with today's exact text, including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only.
  - **(b) Cross-project guard** — still fires on both paths when the data file belongs to a different git repository.
  - **(e) Push flags** — `--no-verify` on the incremental path; `--force --no-verify` on the rewrite path.

- **Existing suites pass and the grep assertion is not weakened.** `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` and `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` pass unchanged in intent; if the `--no-verify` source-grep assertion still exists it is re-pointed (and still asserts the same property) rather than deleted or loosened — if WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z has already replaced it with a behavioural test, no re-point is needed and this clause is satisfied trivially.
  - The `--no-verify` source-grep assertion in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (currently ~:286-305) is re-pointed so it still asserts 'no push line in `src/sync/push.ts` lacks `--no-verify`' — re-pointed, not deleted or loosened. Sibling WL-0MVPUD2S9003H08Z (which would delete it) is still at `idea`.
  - `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` passes unchanged in intent.

- **Testing / validation criterion.** The two currently-uncovered policies in AC2(c) and AC2(d) each gain at least one meaningful test that fails if the policy is swapped between the two paths (negative proof, not just a happy-path assertion).
  - The incremental empty-stage and the rewrite empty-stage tests each fail if the policy is swapped between the two paths; likewise the two missing-file tests.
  - Every new and re-pointed test passes against the **current, pre-refactor** implementation.
  - `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.

## Key Files

- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — incremental-path policy tests and the
  `--no-verify` grep re-point.
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — rewrite-path empty-stage test, exact
  guard-message assertions, explicit `--force` assertion.
- `src/sync/push.ts` — Read only (unchanged): the implementation these tests
  pin.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only: supplies the cross-project guard the
  guard test exercises.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only: supplies `withTempWorktree`, used by the
  real-`git` incremental test.

# Extract shared data-file push preamble helper

Refactor child of WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND (*Deduplicate the worktree/push preamble
shared by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`). Its
sibling *Pin push-path policy divergence with tests* lands the behavioural tests
first; this child performs the dedupe and must leave those tests untouched and
green.

## Why

`gitPushDataFileToBranch` (incremental) and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`
(rewrite) in `src/sync/push.ts` each carry a near-identical preamble:

1. cross-project guard (`assertDataFileInCwdRepo`)
2. `refs/heads/` + `refs/tags/` safety guard
3. `git rev-parse --git-dir`
4. repo-root / repo-relative-path resolution (`getRepoRoot`,
   `getRepoRelativePath`, `path.resolve`)
5. data-file existence check
6. `withTempWorktree(...)`
7. `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`
8. `git add -f`
9. `git diff --cached`
10. `git commit`

A fix to any one of those steps must currently be made twice and can silently
drift.

## Desired change

One **private** helper in `src/sync/push.ts` (working name
`withDataFileInTempWorktree`) owns the preamble and delegates the
mode-specific tail to a callback:

- **Guard + resolve:** `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs rejection,
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot()` / `getRepoRelativePath()` /
  `path.resolve()`, and the existence check.
- **Materialise:** `withTempWorktree(repoRootPath, target, …, { forceOrphan })`,
  `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync`, `add -f`, `diff --cached`.
- **Commit**, then invoke the caller's `run(worktreePath, relativePath, …)` so
  each caller performs only its own push and post-push bookkeeping.

The four documented behavioural differences must stay **explicit options**, not
collapsed:

- `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` resolves as a no-op **without**
  invoking the callback; `'throw'` raises the existing
  `Nothing staged for the rewrite; aborting to avoid an empty ref` message.
- `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'` — `'skip'` returns silently; `'throw'` raises
  `Worklog data file not found: <path>`.
- `forceOrphan: boolean` — `true` only for the rewrite path.
- `skipPrePushHint: boolean` — `true` only for the incremental path, so both
  guard messages stay byte-identical to today.

The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup (`listTrackedFiles` +
`git rm` + `git clean -fdx`) stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback — it
is mode-specific, not preamble.

Both public functions then reduce to: resolve options → call the helper →
mode-specific push. The rewrite path additionally updates
`refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and returns the new tip SHA.

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: no signature change, no behavioural change, no error-message
  change.
- No consumer edits; the `./sync.js` barrel surface is unchanged.
- The helper stays private to `src/sync/push.ts`; `src/sync/worktree.ts` stays a
  data-file-agnostic lifecycle layer and does not learn about data files.
- No scope creep into the duplicate read-side preamble in `src/sync/remote.ts`
  (record it as a separate follow-up if it is worth doing).
- Agent test runs go through `/skill:test` only.

## Risks to keep pinned

- **Empty-stage drift (highest risk).** A single policy applied to both paths
  would either publish nothing while reporting success (rewrite) or turn a
  routine no-change sync into an error (incremental). The sibling's
  negative-proof tests fail if this happens.
- **Guard-message merge.** Collapsing the two messages would drop the
  `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint from the incremental path (or add it where
  it does not belong). The hint is an explicit parameter; the exact-text test
  pins it.
- **Lost `forceOrphan`.** If the helper does not thread `{ forceOrphan: true }`
  through to `withTempWorktree`, the rewrite path fetches the polluted ref
  again — the exact bug the earlier split fixed.
- **Return-type widening.** The rewrite path needs a value from inside the
  callback (tip SHA) while the skip policy produces nothing. The helper's
  generic return must stay honest so the rewrite caller cannot silently drop
  the SHA.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared preamble.** One new private helper (e.g. `withDataFileInTempWorktree`) in `src/sync/push.ts` contains the cross-project guard, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, the repo-root/relative-path resolution, the existence check, and the `withTempWorktree` + copy + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + commit sequence; both `gitPushDataFileToBranch` and `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` are implemented on top of it. Each of those steps appears exactly once in the file (inspection / duplicate-block assertion), and `src/sync/push.ts` gets shorter.
  - The helper owns: `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`, the refs safety guard, `git rev-parse --git-dir`, `getRepoRoot`/`getRepoRelativePath`/`path.resolve`, the existence check, `withTempWorktree` + `ensureDir` + `copyFileSync` + `add -f` + `diff --cached` + `commit`.
  - The four documented differences stay explicit options: `emptyStage: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `missingFile: 'skip' | 'throw'`, `forceOrphan` (rewrite only), `skipPrePushHint` (incremental only).
  - The incremental path's foreign-tracked-file cleanup stays in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`'s callback; the rewrite path still returns the new tip SHA and updates `refs/worklog/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
  - Duplicate-block inspection: none of the ten preamble steps appears twice.

- **Behaviour preserved exactly, proven by test.** Named tests assert, for *both* paths: (a) rejection of `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*` targets with today's message text (including the `Use WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` hint on the incremental path only); (b) the cross-project guard still fires; (c) the empty-stage policy — incremental path resolves without error, rewrite path rejects with `Nothing staged for the rewrite`; (d) the missing-data-file policy — incremental path resolves, rewrite path rejects with `Worklog data file not found`; (e) the push invocation carries `--no-verify` (incremental) and `--force --no-verify` (rewrite).
  - The sibling's tests (empty-stage, missing-file, refs messages, cross-project guard, push flags) pass unchanged and green after the refactor.
  - `{ forceOrphan: true }` is threaded to `withTempWorktree` on the rewrite path only; the pre-push hint appears on the incremental path only; the rewrite path cannot silently drop the tip SHA.

- **Size and structural gate.** `src/sync/push.ts` shrinks (net fewer lines); no file exceeds 1,000 lines; `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` is green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` **unchanged** (no re-baselining); `npm run build` is green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.
  - `src/sync/push.ts` net shorter; no file exceeds 1,000 lines.
  - `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` green with `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` unchanged (no re-baselining).
  - `npm run build` green; `/skill:test` (changed scope) green.

- **No surface change.** The `src/sync.ts` barrel exports are identical (same names, same signatures — asserted by `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`); no consumer edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.
  - Barrel export names and signatures identical; no edits in `src/commands/sync.ts`, `src/commands/doctor.ts`, `src/commands/init.ts` or `src/index.ts`.

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically the `src/sync/push.ts` module header (naming the helper and the two policies) and the `src/sync/push.ts` row/table entry in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` if its description changes. CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the release pipeline).
  - `src/sync/push.ts` module header names the helper and the two mode-specific policies.
  - The `src/sync/push.ts` row in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is updated if the module description changes; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched (release pipeline owns it).

- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
  - Enforced at the dev-push gate (pre-push hook runs `--scope full`).

## Key Files

- `src/sync/push.ts` — new private helper; both public functions rewritten on
  top of it; module header updated.
- `src/sync/worktree.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `withTempWorktree`,
  `listTrackedFiles`, `ensureDir`.
- `src/sync/repo-context.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `assertDataFileInCwdRepo`,
  `getRepoRoot`, `getRepoRelativePath`.
- `src/sync/refs.ts` — Read only (unchanged): `getRemoteTrackingRef` for the
  rewrite path's post-push bookkeeping.
- `src/sync.ts` — Unchanged barrel; verify the exports are identical.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/rewrite-and-force-push.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green).
- `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts` — Read only (must stay green);
  `tests/sync/sync.split-baseline.json` must not be regenerated.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — update the `src/sync/push.ts` row if the module
  description changes.
