# Saturated pre-check refusal carries the derived cooldown

Implements WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX **AC3** (producer answer Q2-A: derive on the
pre-check refusal from the availability payload's held lease, keeping
"refused availability never churns a lease").

## Context

The 429 `retry_after_s` is carried on the admission refusal
(`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts:462`) and the orchestrator decision entry
(`downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:734`) — but the pre-check refuses
BEFORE admission whenever availability reports `available:false`, which is
exactly the state a held foreign lease produces. So the admission `saturated`
arm and its `retryAfterS` deferral rarely run, and the pre-check refusal names
no cooldown at all.

The availability contract already pins `leases[].expiresAt` as epoch
milliseconds (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts:73-87`), read
through a tolerant normaliser — the derivation source exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the availability read reports `available:false` (the state a held foreign lease produces), the pre-check refusal derives `retryAfterS` from the held lease's `leases[].expiresAt` (epoch ms → seconds) and surfaces it on the decision entry exactly like the admission 429 arm does.
- No extra proxy calls: the acquire is still only attempted when the pre-check admits.
- Pinned with a captured payload test (held-lease availability → refusal with the derived cooldown), plus a test that the existing admission-carried `retryAfterS` surface is unchanged.
- A malformed or already-past `expiresAt` clamps to a sane cooldown (>= 0) and never throws on the pre-check path.
- If the live proxy serves `leases: []` while saturated, the derivation degrades to "no cooldown named" and this is reported on the child rather than silently dropped.
- No other dispatch behaviour change, and the full herdr test suite stays green with this change.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` (`:789`) and the returned `DowntimeActiveAuditResult`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `DowntimeActiveAuditResult` (`:782`) gains the cooldown evidence.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — `:710` pre-check consumption, refusal/decision shape.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — the decision entry that carries `retryAfterS` (`:731`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` — `AuditAvailabilityLease.expiresAt` (epoch ms).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.test.ts`, `audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts` — captured-payload pinning.

## Impact

A saturated audit refusal now names its cooldown on the common path, so an operator can tell when the tier re-checks without reading the code.

# Document close-path ownership and lease capability

Implements WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX **AC6** (and gates AC7).

## Context

The four consolidation slices (AC1–AC4) change: who owns the pane-close
record (reaper, not the disabled monitor); how many times availability is
read (once per audit attempt); what a saturated pre-check refusal names (a
derived `retryAfterS` cooldown); and what the coordination check-in
advertises (audit-lease capability, fail-closed). Every surface that
documents the old wiring — code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`,
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and any wiki/docs-site entries — must
describe the new wiring, or a maintainer will trust the disabled monitor
again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (lease protocol + close-path ownership + pre-check cooldown + coordination capability), and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- The "release is guaranteed on every terminal path" claim in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` reflects that the reaper owns the pane-close record and its release discipline.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` records the AC4 fail-closed capability gate for old hosts and the AC3 derived-cooldown on the pre-check refusal.
- The documentation update lands with (or immediately after) the last code slice, so no interim docs claim contradicts the tree.
- The full project test suite must pass with the new changes (parent AC7 gate).

## Key Files

Maintainers and operators read one accurate description of who closes panes, how the cooldown is restored, and why a stale host is refused — no trust in a dead monitor.

# Dispatcher unevenly distributes downtime work across projects

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher is documented to share idle capacity across registered
projects by **global cross-project round-robin** ("no single project can
monopolise the downtime worker"), but measured dispatch history shows the
opposite: on each of the last three nights one project consumed roughly half of
all dispatches in long consecutive runs, while other registered projects with
live coordination entries were dispatched rarely or not at all.

Measured from every project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` on this
machine (rows with a `paneId`, i.e. dispatches that actually produced a pane):

| Night | Total | Distribution | Longest consecutive run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-15 | 47 | AI_Hell 24, ContextHub 22, games_curator 1 | AI_Hell 11, ContextHub 9 |
| 2026-11-16 | 91 | games_curator 35, tce-the-rising 23, ContextHub 19, AI_Hell 14 | games_curator 5, tce-the-rising 5, 4 |
| 2026-11-17 | 96 | **SorraAgents 48**, tce-the-rising 16, games_curator 14, AI_Hell 10, ContextHub 8 | **SorraAgents 9, 8, 8, 6, 4, 3** |

Two further facts sharpen the picture:

- Every SorraAgents dispatch on 2026-11-17 was a **prep-tier** kind (21
  `intake`, 22 `plan`, 5 `risk-effort`) and none was `implement` or `audit`,
  whereas every other project's dispatches that day were dominated by
  `implement`/`audit`.
- The round-robin cursor (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`)
  **is** being written — so this is not a repeat of the "cursor never wired"
  defect (WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK) nor of the "charge at selection, not at
  dispatch" defect (WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN). The residual behaviour is still
  unfair after both fixes landed.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle machine capacity to rotate across every
  project that has dispatchable work, so that a project with a large backlog of
  one stage cannot consume the whole night while other projects' ready work
  waits, and so that standup reports are not dominated by a single project.
- **As a project owner (agent or human) watching a project go undispatched for
  a day**, I want to see *why* my project was skipped — a hold, a deep review
  queue, or a fairness defect — from the dispatch and decision logs, rather
  than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness rule to be enforced by
  the code path that actually chooses what to dispatch, with a test that fails
  when one project wins several consecutive slots while a peer has an
  admissible offer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The dispatch selection path is documented and tested such that, when two or more projects have admissible offers and surplus capacity exists, no project is dispatched more than twice in succession; a failing-first test drives a coordination file with four roots holding interleaved admissible/held offers and asserts the bound.
- The residual bias is identified with evidence and one of the two candidate mechanisms below is either confirmed and fixed, or ruled out with recorded evidence: (a) rotation applies only to the tick's selected root, so when that root's offers are all held the leader falls through the remaining entries in raw coordination-file order; (b) prep-tier offers (`intake`/`plan`/`risk-effort`) are never held by the review-queue, CPU or audit-slot gates while `implement`/`audit` offers are, so a project with a large prep backlog wins every slot on a machine whose other projects have mature implement/audit backlogs.
- A per-project fairness metric is recorded on every dispatch decision (selected root, dispatching root, tick outcome, and the consecutive-run length for the dispatching root) so the distribution can be audited after the fact from `downtime-dispatches.log` or the coordination decision log without replaying logs by hand.
- Fairness accounting does not regress the existing overrides: critical-first dispatch, priority ordering, the review-queue depth gate, the audit slot minimum, the code-freeze split-by-skill, and the host-wide dispatch budget all behave exactly as they do today; each has a test asserting it still wins over round-robin rotation.
- The observed concentration is re-measured after the fix and reported on the work item: over a comparable window with at least three active projects, no project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches, and no project holds a consecutive run longer than the bound in AC1.
- New and updated tests cover the fairness invariant, the two candidate mechanisms, the overrides in AC4, and the fairness metric in AC3.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The producer can trust that a night of idle machine time is shared across every project that has ready work, instead of one project absorbing half the night's dispatches while the others wait.

## Constraints

- **No new scheduler.** Fix the existing leader selection path (`selectLeastRecentlyServed` + the entry loop in `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`); do not introduce per-tier cursors, a second ranking, or a new queue.
- **Preserve every existing gate.** Producer-review, attempt-budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, CPU saturation, audit slot minimum, in-flight and review-queue holds are sequential filters with established semantics (WL-0MWDDHVN and successors) and must not be relaxed, reordered or duplicated to buy fairness.
- **Fail-open fairness.** A cursor read/write failure, a lock timeout or a corrupt cursor file must never block or fail a dispatch; the tick degrades to today's behaviour.
- **On-disk cursor format unchanged.** `{ "<worklogRoot>": "<ISO-8601>" }` in `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`; no migration, so live machine state stays valid.
- **Hot path budget.** No additional `wl` spawns per tick; at most one extra coordination-lock acquisition per consumed offer.
- **Scope guard.** Any additional unfairness found outside the leader selection path (for example the own-backlog fallback tracked by WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG) is recorded as a separate work item, not folded in.

## Existing state

- `selectLeastRecentlyServed` (`downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`) is a pure read: unknown roots sort first, otherwise the oldest timestamp wins, ties broken alphabetically.
- The leader rotates **only the selected root** to the front of the entry list and then iterates the rest in coordination-file order; it returns after the first successful dispatch, so a tick dispatches at most one item.
- The cursor is charged only on a consumed offer (`isConsumedDispatchOutcome`), never at selection — deliberate, per WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN.
- A root that is selected but whose offers are all held is never charged, so it stays first in the rotation indefinitely, and the fall-through order behind it is not round-robin.
- The decision log records per-offer rejections with gate tokens, but not the selected root, the dispatching root, or any run-length accounting; log rotation (500 lines per project) discards the evidence within hours, so past nights cannot be re-audited from the logs.
- Two adjacent defects are already fixed and must not be re-litigated: the cursor was never wired into the dispatch path (WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK) and the post-dispatch charge was dead code (WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN).

## Desired change

A leader selection path in which the rotation is applied to the **whole** ordered candidate set rather than only to the tick's first choice, so that a root whose offers are held cannot silently degrade selection to coordination-file order; plus enough recorded fairness evidence (selected root, dispatching root, run length) to audit any night after the fact.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — Selection is a pure read over the cursor; needs to expose an ordered candidate list (not just the single least-recently-served root) if the fix rotates the whole set.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — The entry rotation, per-offer filter chain and dispatch loop (~490–810); this is where fall-through order is decided and where a run-length bound would be enforced.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `advanceRoundRobinCursor` and the shared `isConsumedDispatchOutcome` charge predicate (~619–666).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-selection.ts` — `orderAdmissibleOffers`, the per-entry drain-aware tie-break that decides which of one entry's offers is tried first.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — The registered-root sweep's own round-robin usage (~420–510); must obey the same fairness rule.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.log-coordination.ts` / `downtime-log-coordination.ts` — Coordination decision entry shape; needs the fairness fields from AC3.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Fair scheduling: global cross-project round-robin* section (~4050–4130); states the guarantee that measurement shows is not met.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: fairness flapping the other way.** Forcing rotation can dispatch low-value prep work ahead of a mature project's ready `implement` item, and can slow a project that is the only one with work. Mitigation: the rotation only reorders *candidates that are already admissible*, and the existing priority/critical overrides still win (AC4).
- **Risk: cursor state carries no "held" information.** A root can look "least recently served" forever because holds are never charged; a naive fix would ping-pong between two starving roots. Mitigation: the four-root interleaved test in AC1 pins the behaviour.
- **Risk: log rotation destroys the evidence mid-investigation.** Mitigation: capture the 2026-11-15/16/17 per-project dispatch-log aggregates on the work item before changing code (the numbers in this brief are that capture).
- **Risk: the measured imbalance is partly legitimate.** A project genuinely holding all dispatchable work *should* be dispatched. Mitigation: AC5 re-measures with at least three active projects and compares against even share, not against zero.
- **Assumption (documented, not confirmed by a producer):** "fair" means an **even share of dispatch slots among projects that have admissible offers**, with critical-first and priority overrides preserved — this is the reading already stated in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, so the brief does not block on it. See the OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.
- **Assumption:** the per-project dispatch logs on this machine are a complete record of dispatches (they are written by the dispatching instance and agree with the round-robin cursor's accounting identity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** removing the own-backlog fallback (WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG) and increasing per-project slot budgets are separate items; this item changes selection fairness only.

## Related work

Automated report (find-related skill):

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** – RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across multiple projects not working (completed)
- **WL-0MNGR0E6E000ZVEQ** – Fix AMPA start-work failure: CONTAINER_PROJECT_ROOT undefined (completed)
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX** – Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: algorithm, dispatch, dispatcher, dispatches, distribute (+12 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: dispatch, dispatcher, dispatches, distribute, evaluate (+9 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: algorithm, dispatch, dispatcher, example, identify (+7 more)

Additional related work identified during intake (read directly, not part of the
automated report):

- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — *Downtime round-robin: post-dispatch cursor charge is dead code, so one project can monopolise the dispatcher.* Same symptom class, adjacent cause (charge point); its own Risks section predicted this residual: "a root that never dispatches is never charged, so it stays first in the rotation indefinitely". This item covers what remained after that fix.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA that first found the cursor was never wired into the dispatch path. The wiring exists now, so this item is not a duplicate.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** (completed) — retired the per-tier `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` second ranking in favour of offer-removal + re-offer; explains why rotation now lives only in the leader entry loop.
- **WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG** (open, low) — whether to remove the own-backlog fallback; a related but separate fairness surface (only 2 of 96 dispatches on 2026-11-17 came from that path).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Fair scheduling: global cross-project round-robin* and *Critical-first dispatch* sections define the guarantee this item measures.
- `docs/dev/release-dispatch-budget-evaluation.md` — the host-wide dispatch budget that must keep precedence over rotation.

Duplicate-work check: performed with `wl search` on `round-robin`, `fairness`,
`dispatcher`, `dispatch imbalance`. No open item covers this gap; the completed
items above are partial overlap only, so the ACs here are scoped to the residual
behaviour rather than rewritten from an existing item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The work item was created by the producer and dispatched automatically by the
herdr downtime worker; no interactive interview round took place in this
session. No question was answered by a human in this session.

- Q: "What does 'fair' mean here — an even share of dispatch slots per project with admissible work, a share weighted by each project's dispatchable backlog depth, or a share weighted by item priority?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (no producer response in this session). Research: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the intent as *global cross-project round-robin* with the explicit goal that "no single project can monopolise the downtime worker", and WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's ACs describe alternating dispatch with a priority override. Working assumption for this brief: even share among projects with admissible offers, priority/critical overrides preserved. If the producer prefers backlog-weighted fairness, AC1/AC5 change but the rest of the brief stands.
- Q: "Is the imbalance the round-robin algorithm being wrong, or a genuine scarcity of admissible work on the other projects?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (self-answered as far as the evidence allows). Research: the two candidate mechanisms in AC2 are both consistent with the measured data; the 2026-11-17 split (all SorraAgents dispatches prep-tier, all other projects' dispatches implement/audit-dominated) points at gate asymmetry at least as much as at ordering. The brief therefore requires confirming or ruling out both mechanisms with evidence rather than assuming one.
- Q: "Should the fix also cover the own-backlog fallback and per-project slot budgets?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: only 2 of 96 dispatches on 2026-11-17 came from `own-backlog-fallback`, and slot budgets are per-project configuration rather than a scheduling rule. Both are out of scope here and already tracked (WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG for the fallback).

### Plan session — 2026-11-17 (agent `plan`, session `herdr-1794934614-3693221-32084`)

This planning run was dispatching-driven (no interactive producer in the
session), so no new interview round took place. The three OPEN QUESTIONs above
were re-reviewed rather than re-asked; each is dispositioned here:

- **Q1 "what does fair mean"** — **NOT BLOCKING.** AC1 pins the concrete
  behaviour (no project dispatched more than twice in succession while a peer
  has an admissible offer and surplus capacity exists) and AC5 pins the
  threshold (no project beyond twice its even share). The working assumption
  (even share among projects with admissible offers, overrides preserved) is
  the documented intent in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and is now
  exercised by the override-precedence regression tests. If the producer wants
  backlog-weighted fairness instead, AC1/AC5 change but the decomposition
  stands.
- **Q2 "algorithm wrong, or genuine scarcity?"** — **RESOLVED BY PLANNING,
  not by assumption.** This is exactly what the diagnosis child
  (WL-0MWKY0R4Z004UU85) must answer with evidence; the plan deliberately does
  not pre-commit to a mechanism.
- **Q3 "also cover own-backlog fallback and slot budgets?"** — **OUT OF
  SCOPE, confirmed.** The parent's scope guard and the existing
  WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG carry the fallback; slot budgets are configuration, not
  a scheduling rule. No child touches them.

**Phasing note.** This item is confined to one package (`packages/herdr`) with
one deployable behaviour, so the phases are test-first slices inside that
component (diagnosis + characterisation → override guards → failing invariant
test → instrumentation → fix → asymmetry resolution → docs → re-measurement)
rather than cross-service vertical slices. Between phases the next child's
description is reviewed and updated before work starts.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17T17:00Z — Plan session decomposed the item into 8 children
  (5 test/verification or instrumentation items before the fix), wired
  dependencies in test-first order, and verified 100% parent AC coverage
  (8/8 ACs mapped, `tree_coverage` review: `proceed`).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WL-0MWKY0R4Z004UU85 — Diagnose residual dispatch-unfairness mechanism | task | — |
| 2 | WL-0MWKY0VF5003ZKRO — Override-precedence regression tests for dispatch fairness | task | — |
| 3 | WL-0MWKY0ZQI004UZXR — Failing-first fairness invariant test (four roots) | task | — |
| 4 | WL-0MWKY141H002LULI — Record per-project fairness metric on dispatch decisions | feature | — |
| 5 | WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O — Rotate the whole admissible candidate set with a run-length bound | feature | 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| 6 | WL-0MWKY1CIJ00462ZD — Resolve the gate-asymmetry finding (mechanism b) | task | 1, 5 |
| 7 | WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD — Docs: the enforced fair-scheduling rule and its metric | docs | 5, 6 |
| 8 | WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K — Re-measure dispatch concentration after the fix | task | 5, 6, 7 |

AC → child map: AC1 → 3, 5, 7 · AC2 → 1, 5, 6 · AC3 → 4 · AC4 → 2 ·
AC5 → 8 · AC6 → 1 (with 2, 3, 4) · AC7 → 7 · AC8 → 8 (final gate).

# Worklog pane startup panic misdiagnoses the cause and prescribes the wrong fix

## User story

As a developer hitting a Worklog pane startup failure, I want the panic message
to name the real cause and the command that actually fixes it, so I do not waste
time on a fix that cannot work.

## Problem

`formatStartupError` in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` treats **every**
"does not provide an export named" error as a stale `@worklog/shared`, printing:

```
The plugin loaded a STALE copy of the shared Worklog code:
  The requested module './downtime-worker.constants.js' does not provide an export named 'DEFAULT_COORDINATION_STALE_WINDOW_MS'
This usually means `packages/shared/dist` was built before the current source.
Rebuild and re-link from the repository root:
      npm run build
```

In the incident that prompted this item the missing module was a **local herdr
module** (`./downtime-worker.constants.js`), not `@worklog/shared`. `npm run
build` at the repo root does **not** compile `packages/herdr`, so the prescribed
fix could never have worked. Two rebuild attempts were made before the real
cause (a bad merge resolution) was found.

The message is well-intentioned but its diagnosis is unconditional, and it is
the only guidance an operator gets.

## Desired change

- Distinguish the specifier: an `@worklog/shared` import → keep the current
  stale-shared guidance; a **relative** import → the plugin's own source and
  build output disagree, so prescribe the herdr package build
  (`npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`, or the `typecheck` script from the
  sibling prevention item).
- Keep the message actionable and short, and never claim a single cause when the
  evidence does not support it.
- Cover both branches with unit tests (sharing/source mismatch vs local module).

## Acceptance criteria

- A local (relative-specifier) missing-export error names `packages/herdr` and
  the herdr package build command that exists today
  (`npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`); it does not name `packages/shared`
  and does not prescribe the repo-root `npm run build`.
- An `@worklog/shared` missing-export error keeps naming the shared package and
  keeps the existing repo-root `npm run build` guidance.
- All three kinds are unit-tested: shared, local, and unattributable/other-bare
  (which must claim no single cause); the non-missing-export branch is unit-
  tested as unchanged too.
- No regression in the existing launcher behaviour (the launcher still exits
  non-zero, and the pane stays open on a TTY so the message can be read).

## Impact

A startup failure now points at the real cause and the command that fixes it,
instead of sending the user down a dead end.

## Discovered from

Diagnosing a Worklog pane startup failure caused by code dropped in merge
`485b764c7`.
## Plan (2026-11-17)

Planning verdict: **no decomposition.** The change is one pure formatter
function in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` plus its tests and docs (~8 h with
overheads), so the plan is the ordered work sequence below rather than child
work items — the same shape as its completed sibling WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q and
its open sibling WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV, neither of which carries children.

### Existing state (verified on the working tree, 2026-11-17)

- `formatStartupError` (`packages/herdr/src/start.ts`) sets `isMissingExport`
  from `/does not provide an export named/i` and emits the **shared-only**
  diagnosis (stale `@worklog/shared`, repo-root `npm run build`). Every other
  failure takes the generic branch (original message + `npm run build` hint +
  `npm install --prefix packages/herdr` fallback).
- The specifier **is** present in the error text and is machine-readable. Node
  22 and tsx 4.21 under `"type": "module"` (as in `packages/herdr`) emit exactly:
  `The requested module './local-partial.mjs' does not provide an export named 'MISSING'`
  — single-quoted specifier, verified against the real resolver by probe.
- Existing coverage: `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` (canonical suite)
  already unit-tests the formatter's shared branch and drives the real launcher
  end-to-end against `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/stale-entry.ts` (plus
  `stale-shared.mjs`), asserting exit code 1 and the diagnostic. That harness is
  reusable verbatim for a relative-specifier case: a sibling
  `local-partial.mjs` + `stale-local-entry.ts` pair reproduces
  `The requested module './local-partial.mjs' does not provide an export named ...`
  under tsx (verified).
- `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` resolves to the herdr package
  (`npm prefix --prefix packages/herdr` → `<repo>/packages/herdr`) and runs its
  `build` script (`build:shared` → `tsc` → copy shortcuts + chmod), so the
  prescribed command exists and does compile the plugin. The repo-root
  `npm run build` compiles only root `src/**` and `packages/shared` — it never
  compiles `packages/herdr`.

### Decisions (recorded; conservative, no producer input required)

- **D1 — prescribe only commands that exist.** The local-branch message
  prescribes `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`; it does **not** reference
  the root `typecheck` script from WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV, because that script does
  not exist yet (`jq .scripts.typecheck package.json` → absent) — naming it
  would reproduce this very defect. AC1 is refined accordingly.
- **D2 — classify by the specifier, not by the module that failed.** Three
  kinds: `shared` (`@worklog/shared…`), `local` (`.`, `..` or an absolute path)
  and `unknown` (no specifier could be extracted, or another bare package). A
  single cause is claimed only for `shared` and `local`.
- **D3 — the launcher contract is unchanged.** `launch()` keeps exit code 1,
  stderr and the TTY-gated keep-open; only the text of the diagnostic changes
  (AC4).
- **D4 — keep the message short.** ≤ ~10 lines per branch, always carrying the
  original error detail verbatim.
- **D5 — no decomposition** (see the verdict above). Test-first ordering is the
  four phases below.

### Message contract (implementation target)

| Kind | Evidence in the error text | Diagnosis | Prescribed command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shared` | specifier begins `@worklog/shared` | stale shared build (text unchanged) | `npm run build` (repo root) |
| `local` | specifier begins `./`, `../` or `/` | the plugin's own module and its build output disagree — names `packages/herdr` | `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` |
| `unknown` | no quoted specifier, or a different bare package | no single cause is claimed; both rebuilds offered | both commands |

The `local` text must state explicitly that the repo-root `npm run build` does
not compile the plugin (the trap that cost the incident two rebuild attempts),
and the `unknown` text must claim neither a stale shared build nor a stale local
build.

### Ordered work sequence (test-first)

1. **Phase 1 — RED tests** in `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` (the
   `formatStartupError` describe block):
   - relative specifier → names `packages/herdr`, contains
     `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`, and contains neither
     `STALE copy of the shared Worklog code` nor `packages/shared/dist`;
   - `@worklog/shared` specifier → shared guidance unchanged (anti-regression);
   - unattributable / other-bare specifier → no single-cause wording, both
     commands present;
   - non-missing-export error → generic branch unchanged (existing assertion);
   - non-`Error` throw → unchanged (existing assertion).

   Verify: the new assertions are RED and every currently-green assertion stays
   green.
2. **Phase 2 — implementation** in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts`:
   - extract the quoted specifier (`/The requested module ['"]([^'"]+)['"]/i`,
     tolerant of both quote styles; an absent match yields `unknown`) and
     classify it;
   - branch the message per the table; leave `launch()`, `waitForDismiss()` and
     the entry-point detection untouched.

   Verify: Phase 1 green; the existing shared-branch and e2e tests stay green.
3. **Phase 3 — end-to-end fixture.** Add
   `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/local-partial.mjs` (exports only a different
   name) and `stale-local-entry.ts` (imports a missing name from
   `./local-partial.mjs`), then extend the `pane launcher (src/start.ts,
   end-to-end)` block: exit code 1, the relative-specifier diagnostic, the herdr
   build command, and prompt exit with stdin closed (the AC4 keep-open
   behaviour is TTY-gated, so the closed-stdin case must not hang).

   Verify: the new e2e case is RED before Phase 2's formatter change and green
   after it.
4. **Phase 4 — docs.** `packages/herdr/README.md` § *Development* (the
   `src/start.ts` note) and § *The Worklog tab closes immediately on open*
   (Troubleshooting): describe both causes, both commands, and that the
   repo-root build does not compile the plugin. Update the `start.ts` header
   comment, which currently presents the stale-shared case as the only cause.

   Verify: no remaining text claims the shared build is the only cause
   (`grep -rin "stale copy of the shared" packages/herdr/`).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` — the formatter and its header comment.
- `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` — formatter unit tests + launcher e2e.
- `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/local-partial.mjs` — new fixture module.
- `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/stale-local-entry.ts` — new fixture entry.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Development + Troubleshooting wording.

### Constraints

- Do not change `launch()`, `waitForDismiss()`, the entry-point detection, the
  TTY gating or the exit code (AC4).
- Do not add a dependency or a new command script: the fix is message text plus
  a specifier classifier.
- Do not weaken the existing shared-branch text — the shared case is still
  correct, and its tests are the anti-regression guard.
- Do not reference the not-yet-existing root `typecheck` script (D1).

### Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — error-text drift across Node versions.** Node 22 quotes the specifier
  with `'`; a future version could change the phrasing. *Mitigation:* the
  extractor tolerates both quote styles and treats an unmatched specifier as
  `unknown`, which claims no single cause — still correct, just less specific.
- **R2 — tsx resolves TS specifiers (`.js` → `.ts`).** The incident specifier was
  a relative `.js` naming a `.ts` source; both are relative, so classification is
  unaffected. *Mitigation:* fixtures use `.mjs` (as the existing shared fixture
  does), which the ESM linker checks without rewriting — verified with tsx 4.21.
- **A1 — `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` is the right prescription.**
  Verified: the herdr `build` script exists and `--prefix` resolves from the repo
  root; it compiles `packages/shared` first, so it repairs both a stale plugin
  build and a stale shared build.
- **A2 — the new assertions are gate-enforced.** `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts`
  is in the canonical suite (`tests`), so no change to `groups.herdr` is needed.

### Out of scope

- Making the repo-root `npm run build` compile `packages/herdr`, and adding a
  root `typecheck` script — WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV.
- Changing the pane-launch manifest or herdr's own error reporting.
- Any change to the `@worklog/shared` link/refresh mechanics — WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q
  owns that.

### Dependencies

- None blocking. `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` exists today, so this
  item does not wait on WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV.
- Once WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV lands, that item's docs may additionally advertise the
  root `typecheck`; no code change here is required.

### Duplicate-work check

No overlapping open or completed item. `wl search` on startup / herdr /
typecheck / "export named" returned: WL-0MWKQ4DO2004C03A (restore the code a bad
merge dropped, completed — the incident, not the diagnostic), WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q
(added the launcher and its shared-only diagnostic, completed — its AC3 covers
only a *shared* export, so its ACs are not satisfied here),
WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4 (missing `marked` package, completed — a different error
class) and WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV (the typecheck gate, open — sibling).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17 — plan pass (agent, non-interactive downtime dispatch): added this
  plan block, the message contract, the four-phase test-first work sequence, Key
  Files, constraints, risks, out-of-scope, dependencies and the duplicate-work
  check. Refined AC1 (the `typecheck` alternative is not prescribed because the
  script does not exist — D1), AC2 (names the existing root command explicitly)
  and AC3/AC4 ("all three kinds"; exit-code plus TTY keep-open). No children
  created (D5).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Should the message prescribe the root `typecheck` script from the
  sibling prevention item, as the Desired change's parenthetical suggests?**
  Answer (agent, documented decision): **No — prescribe
  `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` only.** Evidence:
  `jq .scripts.typecheck package.json` → absent (WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV is
  `plan_complete`, not implemented), so naming it would send the operator to a
  command that does not exist — the exact failure this item fixes. Status:
  resolved by evidence. Reopen only if the producer wants forward references to
  unlanded scripts (not recommended).

- **Q2 — Is a third ("unknown") branch in scope, or should only the shared and
  relative cases change?** Answer (agent, documented decision): **In scope.** The
  Desired change requires "never claim a single cause when the evidence does not
  support it", so a missing-export error from another bare specifier — or one
  whose specifier the extractor cannot read — must hedge. Encoded in AC3.

- **Q3 — Does the plan need child features?** Answer (agent, documented
  decision): **No.** One pure function plus tests and docs (~8 h with
  overheads), and both items of the same shape (WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q,
  WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV) carry zero children. Test-first ordering is the four
  phases above.

- **Q4 — Is there duplicate work in flight?** Answer (agent): **No** — see the
  duplicate-work check above.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MT2GITCX009WUEW** – Remove packages/herdr/src/icons.ts and rewire herdr consumers (completed)
- **WL-0MSG6ODD5002X2OF** – Wire postbuild hook and update docs (completed)
- **WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4** – herdr plugin crashes at startup: Cannot find package 'marked' (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: acceptance, actionable, actually, attempts, bad (+113 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, actionable, actually, attempts, bad (+113 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: actionable, actually, behaviour, build, cannot (+96 more)

data.description:
# No gate type-checks packages/herdr — a broken tree reached main unnoticed

## Problem statement

No automated gate in this repository type-checks `packages/herdr` (or any
`packages/*` project), so a merge that drops symbols while leaving their
consumers in place compiles "green" everywhere and ships. Merge `485b764c7`
did exactly that and reached `main`, breaking the Worklog pane for users until
it was restored by hand (WL-0MWKQ4DO2004C03A).

## Users

- **Maintainer resolving a merge** — needs a broken resolution to fail before
  push, not after release.
- **Producer promoting `dev` → `main`** — needs release promotion to be
  impossible while the tree does not type-check.
- **Worklog pane user** — needs a pane that actually starts, because broken JS
  never reached their machine.

Example user stories:

> As a maintainer, I want a broken TypeScript tree to fail a gate before it is
> pushed, so a bad merge resolution can never ship.

> As a producer, I want `dev` → `main` promotion to refuse a tree that does not
> type-check, so a broken release cannot be cut.

## Existing state (verified 2026-11-17 on the working tree)

| Surface | Type-checks `packages/herdr`? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run build` | **No** | `"build": "npm run build:shared && tsc && node ./scripts/generate-version.cjs"`; root `tsconfig.json` `include: ["src/**/*"]` |
| `npm run postbuild` | **No** | `bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh` (`npm ci` + link only) |
| `packages/herdr` `build` | Yes, but never invoked by root | `"build": "npm run build:shared && tsc && cp src/shortcuts.json dist/shortcuts.json && chmod +x dist/pane-close-cli.js"` |
| pane runtime | **No** | `npx tsx src/start.ts` — esbuild strips types without checking |
| canonical suite | **No** | `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` = `tests`, `packages/shared`, `packages/tui/extensions` — `packages/herdr/src` absent |
| CI | **No** | `cli-tests.yml` and `install-and-smoke-test.yml` run only `npm run build` + `npm test` |
| pre-push hook | **No** | deliberately light; runs the canonical suite, which excludes herdr |
| `implement.py finish` | **No** | changed-scope test selection; tests do not type-check |

No `typecheck` script exists anywhere (`grep '"typecheck"' --include=package.json` → no matches outside `node_modules`).

**An unreachable guard already exists.** `packages/herdr/src/build-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MUFSQMH90086I7W) already shells out to `npx tsc --noEmit` in the package
directory — but it lives under `packages/herdr/src`, and that suite is an
**opt-in** profile (`groups.herdr`) per the producer decision on
WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8. It is therefore never executed by any gate. The gap is one
of *reachability*, not of authoring a check from scratch.

**Baseline is green.** Measured today with `tsc --noEmit`:

| Project | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| root (`tsconfig.json`) | clean, exit 0 | ~15 s |
| `packages/shared` | clean, exit 0 | ~11 s |
| `packages/herdr` | clean, exit 0 | ~16 s |
| `packages/tui` | **no tsconfig exists** | n/a |

So the check can be wired in immediately without a fix-first phase.

## Desired change

1. **One `typecheck` script.** Root `package.json` gains `typecheck` running
   `tsc --noEmit` for root, `packages/shared` and `packages/herdr`. Scope is
   every `packages/*` directory that has a tsconfig — `packages/tui` has none,
   so it is out (see ACs and OPEN QUESTION 1).
2. **Close the emit-on-error hole.** `noEmitOnError: true` in the root,
   `packages/shared` and `packages/herdr` tsconfigs, so a type error leaves
   `dist/` untouched instead of writing loadable-but-broken JS.
3. **Make `npm run build` authoritative.** Root `build` builds `packages/herdr`
   too. This is the cheapest possible release gate: the ship pipeline already
   runs `npm run build` (via `regenerate-version.js`), so a herdr type error
   blocks promotion with no change to the release scripts.
4. **Join the canonical suite.** Add the `typecheck` command to
   `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands`, so the dev-push hook, audit F3 and
   the ship release gate all inherit the check. `groups.herdr` is left intact.
   The pre-push hook template is **not** modified — its lightweight contract
   holds because the check rides inside the full suite it already runs.
5. **CI.** A type-check step/job in `install-and-smoke-test.yml` (runs on PR and
   on push to `main`) sequenced **before** `npm run build`, plus a path-filtered
   job in `cli-tests.yml` so a PR touching `packages/**` or `src/**` gets fast
   feedback.
6. **Reconcile the orphaned guard.** `build-guard.test.ts` becomes redundant
   with the new script but is left in place (it still guards the opt-in herdr
   profile); the docs state that `npm run typecheck` is the single source of
   truth and the test is a secondary, profile-local assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `typecheck` npm script exists at the repo root and exits non-zero on any
  diagnostic from root, `packages/shared` and `packages/herdr`; it covers every
  `packages/*` directory that contains a tsconfig.
- CI fails on a deliberate type error in `packages/herdr/src` — verified with a
  temporary throwaway commit reverted on the same branch before merge.
- CI fails on a deliberate type error in root `src` — verified the same way.
- `npm run build` at the repo root fails on a type error in `packages/herdr`,
  and `noEmitOnError: true` is set in the root, `packages/shared` and
  `packages/herdr` tsconfigs so `dist/` is unchanged after a forced error
  (verified by mtime comparison).
- The canonical full suite (`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands`) includes the
  typecheck, so the dev-push hook, audit F3 and the ship release gate inherit it
  with no change to the pre-push hook template; `groups.herdr` is unchanged.
- Documentation in `docs/dev/` (alongside `test-suite-baseline.md` § Test gates
  and `pre-push-hook.md`) records the new gate, its scope, its deliberate
  exclusions and how it relates to the opt-in herdr test profile.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A TypeScript type error now fails the build, CI and the release gate instead of
silently reaching a release, so a broken tree can no longer ship to users.

## Constraints

- Do **not** re-litigate the producer decision in WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8 (herdr
  *tests* excluded from the canonical suite). This item is about
  **type-checking**, which is a separate gate and runs no tests.
- `groups.herdr` in `.pi/test-config.json` stays intact — only `suiteCommands`
  is extended.
- Keep the pre-push hook lightweight per `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`: the check
  rides inside the full suite, the hook template stays byte-identical to
  `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` and `tests/fixtures/pre-push-hook.expected.sh`.
- "The herdr group already covers it" is not an acceptable outcome — an opt-in
  profile that no gate runs is the bug being fixed.
- Type-checking `packages/tui/extensions` requires authoring a tsconfig for a
  tree that only ever runs under `tsx`; that is out of scope (OPEN QUESTION 1).

## Decisions and assumptions

Recorded as decisions taken during intake with a recommended option; the
producer may overrule any of them at review.

- **D1 — typecheck scope excludes `packages/tui`.** No tsconfig exists there and
  the tree is `tsx`-only; adding one is a separate change. AC wording ("every
  `packages/*` with a tsconfig") already encodes this.
- **D2 — `noEmitOnError: true` applied to all three tsconfigs**, not only
  herdr. Baseline is green for all three, so the risk is near-zero and the hole
  is closed everywhere at once.
- **D3 — enforcement rides the canonical suite**, not a bespoke pre-push rule.
  This reuses four existing gates (implement finish, dev-push, audit, ship) and
  leaves the hook contract untouched.
- **D4 — `build-guard.test.ts` is kept, not deleted.** Deleting a passed guard
  is churn; documenting the precedence of `npm run typecheck` is enough.
- **A1 — assumption:** the producer wants the check in the *release* path, which
  is satisfied by `npm run build` because `regenerate-version.js` already
  invokes it.
- **A2 — assumption:** ~16–45 s added to the full suite (three serial
  `tsc --noEmit` runs, measured today) is acceptable against a suite that
  currently budgets 2–4 minutes and a `timeoutPerCommand` of 3600 s.

## Risks and mitigations

- **R1 — CI path filters miss the new job.** `cli-tests.yml` only triggers on a
  listed path set; a new job needs `packages/**`, `tsconfig*.json` and
  `package.json` in its filter. Mitigation: explicit filter entries, plus the
  unfiltered `install-and-smoke-test.yml` job as backstop.
- **R2 — `noEmitOnError` changes build semantics** for anyone relying on partial
  emit from a red tree. Mitigation: tree is green today; no consumer builds from
  a red tree by design.
- **R3 — suite wall-time and ratchet interference.** Adding ~16–45 s to the full
  suite could interact with the measured ratchet projects. Mitigation: the
  typecheck is a plain command in `suiteCommands`, not a vitest file, so it runs
  outside the serialised measured group.
- **R4 — scope creep.** Type-checking `packages/tui/extensions`, adding
  `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, or extending the herdr group to the canonical
  suite are *not* in scope; record them as linked follow-up work items instead.
- **R5 — two overlapping mechanisms** (`typecheck` script and
  `build-guard.test.ts`) drift apart. Mitigation: D4 documents precedence and
  the docs section names the single source of truth.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — add `typecheck`; extend `build` to compile `packages/herdr`.
- `tsconfig.json` — `noEmitOnError: true`.
- `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` — `noEmitOnError: true`.
- `packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` — `noEmitOnError: true`.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — add the typecheck command to `suiteCommands`;
  `groups.herdr` untouched.
- `.github/workflows/install-and-smoke-test.yml` — type-check step before build.
- `.github/workflows/cli-tests.yml` — path-filtered type-check job.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — new gate row/section under § Test gates.
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` — note that the typecheck rides the full suite.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — note that `npm run build` now covers the package.
- `packages/herdr/src/build-guard.test.ts` — comment pointing at the new
  authoritative script (no behavioural change).

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKQ4DO2004C03A** — Restore code dropped by bad merge `485b764c7`
  (completed). The incident this item prevents recurring; that item fixed the
  symptom, this one closes the gate.
- **WL-0MWKQ50CT0022PGK** — Worklog pane startup panic misdiagnoses the cause
  and prescribes the wrong fix (open). Sibling finding from the same diagnosis;
  its "run `npm run build`" advice is only true once D3 lands.
- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — producer decision making the herdr *test* suite an
  opt-in profile. Respected; this item gates *types*, not tests.
- **WL-0MUFSQMH90086I7W** — Fix herdr plugin build: import `PaneLifecycleKind`
  in `downtime-worker.ts` (completed). Origin of `build-guard.test.ts`.
- **WL-0MSNXXA6O001ESB5**, **WL-0MSA9AM8S003UE7O**, **WL-0MT5YFJ8A0059SDJ** —
  prior one-off herdr build/type failures fixed by hand. Each is evidence that
  the missing gate costs a manual cycle per occurrence.
- **WL-0MSG6ODD5002X2OF** — Wire postbuild hook and update docs (completed).
  Owns the current `postbuild` → `install-herdr.sh` behaviour touched by D3.
- **WL-0MVPW5NNN00389BM** — Fix stale `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` drift
  (completed). Relevant because `install-herdr.sh` runs `npm ci` there.

Potentially related docs (paths):

- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — § Test gates, canonical suite definition,
  and § "The herdr package suite is a separate, opt-in gate".
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` — the hook contract that must stay lightweight.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — package build/install instructions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Intake was dispatched non-interactively (herdr downtime worker), so no operator
was available to answer live. Each question below records the research that
narrowed it, the recommended option taken as a documented intake decision, and
its status.

- **Q1 — Should `packages/tui/extensions` be type-checked?**
  Answer (agent, pending producer confirmation): **No, not in this item.**
  Research: `find packages/tui -name tsconfig*` → no match; the tree has only
  `packages/tui/extensions/package.json` and is executed exclusively through
  `tsx` (see `install-and-smoke-test.yml` smoke test). Adding a tsconfig for a
  `tsx`-only tree is a separate design change and would pull Pi runtime types
  into scope. Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — producer may overrule into scope.
  Source: repo inspection, 2026-11-17.

- **Q2 — Where must enforcement live: pre-push hook, CI, or the canonical
  suite?** Answer (agent, pending producer confirmation): **the canonical suite
  plus CI**, exploiting the fact that the ship pipeline already runs
  `npm run build` (`regenerate-version.js:76`). Research: `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`
  states the hook is deliberately light and its template is byte-locked across
  three artifacts, so adding a bespoke step there would mean editing
  `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`, `.githooks/pre-push` and the fixture together.
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — producer may prefer an explicit pre-push step.
  Source: repo inspection, 2026-11-17.

- **Q3 — Is the existing `build-guard.test.ts` sufficient, and can this item be
  closed as a duplicate?** Answer (agent): **No.** Research: the test does run
  `npx tsc --noEmit` in `packages/herdr`, but `packages/herdr/src` is absent
  from `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` and is only reachable via the
  opt-in `groups.herdr` profile (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8), so no gate executes it.
  Status: resolved by research — the gap is reachability, not authoring.
  Source: `.pi/test-config.json`, `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` § "The herdr
  package suite is a separate, opt-in gate".

- **Q4 — Does the baseline currently pass, i.e. is a fix-first phase needed?**
  Answer (agent): **No fix-first phase needed.** Research: `tsc --noEmit`
  exits 0 for root (~15 s), `packages/shared` (~11 s) and `packages/herdr`
  (~16 s) on the working tree at intake time. Status: resolved by research.
  Source: local runs, 2026-11-17.

- **Q5 — Is duplicate work already in flight?** Answer (agent): **No.**
  Research: `wl search` on `typecheck`, `type check`, `tsc noEmit`,
  `noEmitOnError`, `herdr-build` returned only prior one-off herdr build fixes
  (all `completed`) and the incident-restore item WL-0MWKQ4DO2004C03A. No open
  item adds a type-checking gate. Status: duplicate check performed — no
  overlapping open or completed item found.

# Rotate the whole admissible candidate set, with a run-length bound

Parent: **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**. Covers parent **AC1** and mechanism **(a)** of
**AC2**; the parent's *Desired change* section is this item's specification.

## Goal

Make the rotation apply to the **whole** ordered candidate set rather than only
to the tick's first choice, so a root whose offers are all held cannot silently
degrade selection to coordination-file order, and enforce a consecutive-run
bound so one root cannot hold the dispatcher for several slots while a peer has
an admissible offer.

## Scope

- Selection currently returns a single least-recently-served root
  (`selectLeastRecentlyServed`) and the leader splices only that root to the
  front, then walks the rest in file order. Expose an **ordered candidate list**
  (least-recently-served first, unknown roots first, ties alphabetical) and have
  the leader order its whole entry list from it, so held-offer fall-through is
  still round-robin.
- Enforce the bound: while a peer root has an admissible offer and surplus
  capacity exists, a root that has already dispatched twice in succession is
  deferred behind the next admissible root. Use the run-length tracking from the
  fairness-metric sibling — do not introduce a second accounting source.
- Apply the same rule to the registered-root sweep's starting-root order, so the
  two paths cannot drift.
- Keep the selection call a **pure read**: only a consumed offer charges the
  cursor, via the shared `isConsumedDispatchOutcome` predicate.

## Constraints

- **No new scheduler.** Fix the existing leader selection path; no per-tier
  cursors, no second ranking, no new queue.
- **Preserve every gate.** Producer-review, attempt-budget, non-terminal
  cooldown, code-freeze, CPU saturation, audit slot minimum, in-flight and
  review-queue holds stay sequential filters with unchanged semantics; they must
  not be relaxed, reordered or duplicated to buy fairness.
- **Fail-open fairness.** A cursor read/write failure, lock timeout or corrupt
  run-length source must never block or fail a dispatch — the tick degrades to
  today's behaviour.
- **On-disk cursor format unchanged.** `downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` keeps
  `{ "<worklogRoot>": "<ISO-8601>" }`; no migration.
- **Hot path budget.** No additional `wl` spawn per tick; at most one extra
  coordination-lock acquisition per consumed offer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- (parent AC1) The dispatch selection path is documented and tested such that, when two or more projects have admissible offers and surplus capacity exists, no project is dispatched more than twice in succession; a failing-first test drives a coordination file with four roots holding interleaved admissible/held offers and asserts the bound.
- Selection exposes an ordered candidate list (or an equivalent deterministic whole-set ordering) and the leader orders its entire entry list from it, so a selected-but-fully-held root no longer leaves fall-through in raw coordination-file order.
- The four-root failing test from the sibling test item passes, with no root dispatched more than twice in succession while a peer has an admissible offer and surplus capacity exists.
- The registered-root sweep's starting-root ordering obeys the same fairness rule and has its own test.
- Selection remains a pure read: a tick that selects a root and consumes nothing leaves the cursor file byte-identical, asserted by test.
- Every existing override still wins: the override-precedence regression tests from the sibling test item stay green.
- Fail-open is covered by test: a corrupt/missing cursor or run-length source degrades to today's ordering and still dispatches.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — add the ordered-candidate-list read; keep the cursor format
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — whole-set entry ordering, run-length deferral, dispatch loop
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — sweep starting-root order
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `advanceRoundRobinCursor` / `isConsumedDispatchOutcome` charge contract
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — entry shape / file order
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.test.ts` — selection unit tests
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-leader.test.ts` — leader-path tests

## Impact

Users can queue work across several projects and trust the dispatcher to rotate fairly across them all — every project with queued work gets its turn, and no project can take more than two consecutive dispatch slots while another has work waiting.

# Resolve the gate-asymmetry finding (mechanism b)

Parent: **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**. Completes parent **AC2** (mechanism (b):
*confirmed and fixed, or ruled out with recorded evidence*).

## Goal

Act on the diagnosis sibling's verdict for mechanism (b): the asymmetry in
which gates hold prep-tier offers (`intake` / `plan` / `risk-effort`) but not
`implement` / `audit` offers. Either the asymmetry contributes to the measured
concentration and is addressed within the leader selection path, or it is
recorded as not a fairness defect (a legitimate scarcity signal) with evidence.

## Scope

Exactly one of these is delivered, chosen by the diagnosis verdict — the choice
and its rationale are recorded on the parent item:

- **Ruled out** (the asymmetry does not starve roots that have admissible work,
  because a root with only held offers has no admissible offer by definition):
  record the evidence, the reasoning and the log excerpts. No code change.
- **Confirmed and fixable in the selection path**: implement the ordering-side
  fix — never by relaxing, reordering or duplicating a gate. A root whose only
  offers are prep work may not monopolise slots while peer roots have
  admissible implement/audit offers; the deferral from the fix sibling's
  run-length bound is the intended mechanism. Add tests.
- **Confirmed but a policy question** (which gates should hold prep work, or
  whether fairness should be weighted by backlog depth rather than by
  admissible-offer parity): do NOT change policy in this item. Record the
  decision needed, mark the parent as needing producer review, and file a
  separate work item for the policy change.

## Constraints

- Preserve every existing gate: producer-review, attempt-budget, non-terminal
  cooldown, code-freeze, CPU saturation, audit slot minimum, in-flight and
  review-queue holds keep their current semantics (parent Constraints).
- Do not fold in the own-backlog fallback (WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG) or per-project
  slot budgets — separate items (parent scope guard).

## Acceptance Criteria

- (parent AC2, mechanism b) The residual bias is identified with evidence and one of the two candidate mechanisms is either confirmed and fixed, or ruled out with recorded evidence — here, mechanism (b): prep-tier offers (`intake`/`plan`/`risk-effort`) are never held by the review-queue, CPU or audit-slot gates while `implement`/`audit` offers are, so a project with a large prep backlog wins every slot on a machine whose other projects have mature implement/audit backlogs.
- The mechanism-(b) verdict from the diagnosis item is addressed by exactly one of: a code change with tests, a recorded rule-out with evidence, or a recorded policy question plus a separate work item and a producer-review flag on the parent.
- If code changes: the change is confined to the leader selection path (ordering and deferral) and no gate is relaxed, reordered or duplicated — asserted by the override-precedence regression tests staying green.
- If code changes: a test pins the concrete asymmetry case — a root with only prep offers must not win every slot while a peer root holds an admissible implement or audit offer.
- If ruled out or escalated: the evidence, the reasoning and the affected log excerpts are recorded in a comment on WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9.
- No behaviour change to the own-backlog fallback or to per-project slot budgets.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — per-offer filter chain and dispatch loop
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — review-queue / audit-slot / CPU gate predicates
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-selection.ts` — drain-aware tie-break (prep-first) inside one entry
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.terminal-reason.ts` — hold-reason precedence
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-leader.test.ts` — leader-path tests

## Impact

Once a project has a mature implement or audit item ready, a peer project with a large preparation (intake/plan/risk-effort) backlog can no longer take every dispatch slot: the dispatcher now serves the ready implement/audit work within two slots, so idle machine time is shared instead of being dominated by prep-only work.

# Re-measure dispatch concentration after the fix

Parent: **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**. Covers parent **AC5**, and verifies AC1 in
production rather than only in tests.

## Goal

Prove the fix works on the live machine, over a comparable window, and report
the numbers on the parent work item. The baseline is the pre-fix capture in the
parent brief (2026-11-15/16/17 aggregates and run lengths).

## Scope

- Collect the same per-project aggregate from every projection's
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (rows with a `paneId`) for a window with at
  least three active projects, plus the run lengths and the kind mix.
- Compare against the even share of dispatch slots among projects that had
  admissible offers.
- Re-derive the distribution from the fairness metric on the decision log and
  confirm it agrees with the dispatch log (the accounting identity).
- Report on WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9: the table, the longest consecutive runs, the
  kind mix per project, and an explicit pass/fail against the thresholds.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement; no dispatcher behaviour change in this item.
- Log rotation (500 lines per project) discards evidence within hours — capture
  the aggregates promptly and record them on the item as soon as they are read.
- If the window has fewer than three active projects, say so and either extend
  the window or record the measurement as inconclusive rather than declaring
  success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- (parent AC5) The observed concentration is re-measured after the fix and reported on the work item: over a comparable window with at least three active projects, no project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches, and no project holds a consecutive run longer than the bound in AC1.
- (parent AC8) Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, verified at the parent's final gate once every sibling has landed.
- A comparable window with at least three active projects is measured, with the per-project dispatch counts, the longest consecutive runs, and the per-project kind mix reported on WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9.
- No project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches in that window, and no project holds a consecutive run longer than the bound asserted by the fairness-invariant test.
- The distribution derived from the decision-log fairness metric agrees with the dispatch-log aggregates, confirming the accounting identity end to end.
- If either threshold is missed, the report records the evidence, the suspected cause, and a follow-up work item rather than closing the measurement as a pass.
- The measurement window (dates, project count) and the counting rules are stated so the result can be reproduced.

## Key Files

- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (per project; read-only)
- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (per project; read-only)
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` — cursor state at the window boundary
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-entries.ts` — dispatch-row shape (`paneId`, `selectionPath`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — decision-entry fairness fields

## Outcome (2026-11-19)

**Inconclusive — the fix is not running on the live machine.** Measured window
2026-11-19T12:22:49Z → 14:16Z: 4 active projects, 8 dispatches, even share 2.00,
AI_Hell 4 (2.00x, longest run 2), SorraAgents 2, ContextHub 1, games_curator 1;
longest run overall 2. Both thresholds are only *touched*, on a sample too small
to mean anything — and the regime check fails: the live downtime worker is a
long-lived `tsx src/start.ts` pane started 2026-11-18T15:39Z, before the fairness
metric (22:41Z) and the fixes (12:22Z / 12:46Z), so no decision entry in any
project's coordination log carries the `selectedRoot` / `dispatchingRoot` /
`consecutiveRunLength` fields the accounting identity needs. The same rules on
the immediately preceding pre-fix window (00:00Z–12:22Z, 13 dispatches, 5
projects) do show the defect — SorraAgents 6, 2.31x even share — confirming the
method works. Counting rules are recorded in
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`; the full report is a comment on
WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9. Follow-up **WL-0MWNN84HO004DXQU** restarts the dispatcher
and re-runs the measurement.

## Impact

A reader of the parent brief can now see the post-fix numbers, the exact counting
rules and an explicit "inconclusive, not a pass" verdict instead of a false
all-clear, because the report refuses to claim success while the live dispatcher
is still running pre-fix code.

# Add startOn (earliest start date/time) to work items

## Goal

Give every work item a first-class **`startOn`** field — the earliest date/time at which the item may proceed — and make every CLI and Herdr-plugin **search surface filter out not-yet-started items by default**. Today scheduling is unenforceable: the only signal is a `[run-not-before 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z]` prefix baked into the title, which nothing filters on, which agents must parse by hand, and which pollutes titles permanently.

## Problem statement

Worklog has no structural scheduling dimension for temporal gates. Downtime-ordered work items encode their earliest-start date in the title text, and nothing enforces or filters on it. This means dispatchers can fire agents before measurement windows are valid, and restarts can silently void mid-flight windows.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher agents** — need a reliable `startOn` signal to know when an item is eligible for dispatch.
- **Human operators** — need `wl list`/`wl search`/`wl next` to respect temporal scheduling without manual date parsing.
- **Herdr worklist users** — need to see not-yet-started items read-only with a "not started until" marker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data model.** `startOn` is stored per work item as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, exposed in every JSON surface (`show`, `list`, `search`, `next`, `recent`, `in_progress`, dependency listings). **Default = the item's `createdAt`** when omitted, including on import of legacy JSONL/Git data that has no field (back-compat is the default, never "blocked").
- **AC2 — CLI authoring.** `wl create --start-on <ISO-8601>` and `wl update <id> --start-on <ISO-8601>` (offset accepted, normalised to UTC); `--start-on ""` clears it back to `createdAt`. Invalid values fail with an actionable message. `wl show <id>` is **never** filtered — an item is always retrievable by id.
- **AC3 — Default filtering in searches.** `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future. An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before <ISO>`) shows them, marked as not yet started in both text and JSON output. `in_progress` items are never filtered out (a started item has already started).
- **AC4 — Herdr plugin parity.** Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default filter, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr worker. Surface not-yet-started items **read-only** in the worklist with a "not started until <date>" marker, following the existing held-items banner convention (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR), and never clear or alter their state.
- **AC5 — Claim guard (defence in depth).** Setting an item to `in_progress` (or any claim path) on a future `startOn` is refused with a machine-readable reason (`start_on_not_reached`) unless an explicit, auditable override is passed; the override writes a comment naming the actor and the reason. The guard must not fire for `createdAt`-defaulted items.
- **AC6 — Migration and sync.** A documented, idempotent migration sets `startOn = createdAt` for existing items (`docs/migrations/`); `doctor` reports a mismatch; JSONL export/import and Git sync round-trip the field; cross-project edges (foreign ids) are unaffected; two-way sync never resurrects a stale value.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit and integration coverage for: default = `createdAt`; future-filtered out of every search surface listed in AC3; opt-in shows them marked; `--start-on` set/clear; claim refused and overridden; legacy JSONL import back-fill; sync round-trip; a frozen-clock test (no wall-clock flakiness).
- **AC8 — Docs and help.** `CLI.md`, `DATA_FORMAT.md`, `API.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and the relevant skill docs updated; `wl create --help` / `wl update --help` describe the field and its default.
- **AC9 — Performance.** An index on `startOn` (or an equivalent query plan) so `list`/`search`/`next` stay within the existing benchmarks on the current store size; record the before/after figures.

## Impact

Users can now schedule work items to become available at a specific future time, ensuring that time-gated measurements and scheduled tasks are not dispatched before their measurement windows are valid.

## Constraints and non-goals

- **Non-goals:** a scheduler or queueing engine, recurrence, timezone UI, automatic re-anchoring of dates, calendar integration.
- Do not repurpose the existing `assignee` hold, `dependencies` or `blocked` status: `startOn` is temporal, dependencies are causal, the assignee hold is an operator claim. All three must compose (an item can be dependency-ready, unheld and still not-yet-started).
- UK English throughout; schema changes ship with migration + docs in the same change; no breaking change to existing JSON consumers (additive field, defaulted).
- Test discipline: the full suite through the project's test skill, and no direct test invocations outside it.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — Add `startOn` to `WorkItem`, `CreateWorkItemInput`, `UpdateWorkItemInput`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Add `startOn` column to the `workitems` table DDL and bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`; include the field in every JSONL export/import row projection
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — Add the idempotent back-fill migration (`startOn = createdAt` for existing rows) and bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/commands/create.ts` — Add the `--start-on <ISO-8601>` option, offset-accepted + normalised to UTC, defaults to `createdAt`
- `src/commands/update.ts` — Add `--start-on <ISO-8601>` (`""` clears back to `createdAt`); host the claim guard on the `--status in_progress` transition
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Default `startOn` exclusion plus `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before <ISO>` opt-in with a not-yet-started marker in text and JSON
- `src/commands/search.ts` — Same default exclusion + opt-in as `list`

- `docs/API.md` — Document `startOn` in every JSON surface
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Document `startOn` scheduling and the claim guard
- `docs/migrations/` — Add the migration note

## Existing state

- No `startOn` field exists anywhere in the codebase.
- Current practice: `[run-not-before YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ]` prefix in item titles, parsed manually by agents.
- Items created 2026-11-18 from the `llm` abort-class remediation chain (`LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP`) encode scheduling in titles.

## Definition of done

A `llm`-style dated work item created with `--start-on 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z` is invisible to `wl next`, `wl search`, `wl list` and the Herdr worklist until that instant, visible with `--include-not-started`, retrievable by id, claimable only after the instant (or by explicit audited override), and survives export/import and a restart unchanged.

## Related work

- LP-0MWM0B7IQ008W2FP — `llm` abort-class remediation chain (explicitly scheduled by title dates; blocked on this feature)
- WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR — Held-items banner convention (reference for Herdr worklist UI marker)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** `startOn` invites adjacent scheduling features (recurrence, calendar, timezone UI, auto re-anchoring). Mitigation: non-goals are explicit above; extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Risk (silent behaviour change):** filtering by default could hide items an operator expects to see. Mitigation: the default is `createdAt`, so every existing item is already "started" and stays visible — the filter only bites on newly authored dates; `--include-not-started` is the escape hatch and not-yet-started items are surfaced read-only in the worklist rather than hidden.
- **Risk (clock flakiness):** future/past comparisons against wall-clock make tests non-deterministic. Mitigation: inject the clock through the shared predicate; AC7 requires a frozen-clock test.
- **Risk (sync resurrection):** a two-way sync could resurrect a stale `startOn` from the remote. Mitigation: AC6 requires two-way sync to never resurrect a stale value, covered by a sync round-trip test.
- **Risk (performance regression):** a non-indexed `startOn` predicate on every search surface could slow `list`/`search`/`next`. Mitigation: AC9 requires an index (or an equivalent query plan) with recorded before/after benchmarks.
- **Assumption:** `createdAt` is always present and non-empty on every existing row, so "default = `createdAt`" needs no fallback beyond the migration back-fill.
- **Assumption:** `startOn` composes with existing gates (dependency readiness, assignee hold, `needsProducerReview`) rather than replacing any of them — the new filter is an additional sequential filter.
- **Assumption:** the downtime dispatcher and `llm`-style dated items are the first consumers; no other project relies on title-embedded dates programmatically.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions — the seed context (work item description) provides sufficient detail for a clear brief. The description was authored by the downtime dispatcher and contains a complete spec with 9 acceptance criteria, constraints, and definition of done.

- **Q3 (plan → producer).** "Should existing `[run-not-before …]` title prefixes

# `isNotStarted` predicate, frozen-clock harness and perf baseline

## Goal

Deliver the shared "is this item not yet started?" predicate that every later
`startOn` slice consumes, together with the deterministic test harness that
keeps its comparisons off the wall clock, and the performance baseline recorded
*before* any filtering or index lands.

This is the test-first foundation slice: it ships code, tests and a recorded
baseline, and changes no CLI or Herdr behaviour.

## Context

`startOn` does not exist yet. Everything else in this epic (schema, authoring,
default filtering, the claim guard, Herdr parity) reads the predicate defined
here, so it lands first and is depended on by all siblings.

## Impact

Work items scheduled for a future date now have one deterministic, test-verified definition of "not yet started", so they become available exactly at their start instant on every surface and no clock-dependent flakiness can make a future item appear early or hide a started one.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Predicate and harness

- [ ] `isNotStarted(item, now)` is exported from
  `packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` and published via the existing
  `@worklog/shared/predicates` subpath (the root `@worklog/shared` entry is a
  frozen surface — never add an export there).
- [ ] Effective start instant resolution is `startOn ?? createdAt`, so the
  default is `createdAt` and every pre-existing item is already "started"
  (back-compat is the default, never "blocked").
- [ ] `now` is an explicit parameter (milliseconds) — no `Date.now()` call
  inside the predicate, so tests are deterministic.
- [ ] A shared frozen-clock test helper is added (e.g.
  `tests/helpers/frozen-clock.ts`) and used by every new `startOn`
  test in this epic.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `startOn` in the future → not started; `startOn` in the
  past → started; `startOn` exactly equal to `now` → started (boundary is
  inclusive); `startOn` absent with past `createdAt` → started; `startOn`
  absent with future `createdAt` → not started; `startOn` absent and
  `createdAt` absent → started; unparseable `startOn` → started (fail-open:
  an unreadable value must never hide an item).
- [ ] The predicate handles ISO-8601 with a UTC offset (`+01:00`) and a `Z`
  suffix identically.

### Performance baseline

- [ ] Baseline `list` / `search` / `next` latency is measured on the existing
  large-db harness (`packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts`) and the
  figures are recorded in `docs/benchmarks/start_on_filter_baseline.md` with
  the store size and the measurement method.

### Non-goals

- No schema change, no CLI flag, no Herdr change in this slice.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** Unit and integration coverage for: default = `createdAt`; future-filtered out of every search surface listed in AC3; opt-in shows them marked; `--start-on` set/clear; claim refused and overridden; legacy JSONL import back-fill; sync round-trip; a frozen-clock test (no wall-clock flakiness).
- [ ] **AC9 — Performance.** An index on `startOn` (or an equivalent query plan) so `list`/`search`/`next` stay within the existing benchmarks on the current store size; record the before/after figures.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/predicates.ts` — add the `isNotStarted` export
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` — existing predicate home for reference
- `tests/helpers/frozen-clock.ts` — new frozen-clock helper
- `packages/shared/src/predicates.test.ts` — new unit tests
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — baseline harness
- `docs/benchmarks/start_on_filter_baseline.md` — recorded baseline

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice.

## Deliverables

- `isNotStarted` predicate with injectable clock, exported via the predicates subpath.
- Frozen-clock test helper used by all later `startOn` tests.
- Recorded pre-filter performance baseline.
