# `startOn` data model, schema migration and sync round-trip

## Goal

Add `startOn` as a first-class stored field: a SQLite column, the type and
field-registry entries, an idempotent back-fill migration for existing rows, a
`doctor` mismatch check, and a JSONL export/import + Git sync round-trip that
never resurrects a stale value.

This is the vertical data slice — schema through to persisted bytes and back.

## Context

`startOn` does not exist anywhere in the codebase today. `SCHEMA_VERSION` is
`9` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`) and
`CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is `'9'` (`src/migrations/index.ts`); both must be
bumped by exactly one step, reconciled in the same change. Scheduling is
currently encoded as a `[run-not-before …]` title prefix that nothing enforces.

Depends on the `isNotStarted` predicate slice for the shared clock-injectable
predicate and the frozen-clock test harness.

## Impact

Scheduled work is now a stored, indexed field that defaults to when the item was created, so an item can carry a real future start time that survives export, import and Git sync and that `wl doctor` can verify — instead of a date hidden in the title that nothing enforces.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Data model

- [ ] `startOn` is added to `WorkItem`, `CreateWorkItemInput` and
  `UpdateWorkItemInput` as an optional ISO-8601 UTC string in
  `packages/shared/src/types.ts`.
- [ ] `startOn` is added to `VALID_FIELDS` in `packages/shared/src/fields.ts`
  so generic field reads/writes see it.
- [ ] A `startOn TEXT` column is added to the `workitems` table DDL in
  `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`, with `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped.
- [ ] An index on `startOn` (or a documented equivalent query plan) is created
  so the default-filter query keeps using an index rather than a table scan.
- [ ] **`startOn` is always populated on write** — it is stored as the
  effective instant (`startOn ?? createdAt`), so queries compare a single
  non-null column and never need `COALESCE` over two columns. A `NULL`
  `startOn` is read as `createdAt` for back-compat.
- [ ] **Default = the item's `createdAt`** when omitted, including on import of
  legacy JSONL/Git data that has no field (back-compat is the default, never
  "blocked").

### Migration and doctor

- [ ] An idempotent migration is added to `src/migrations/index.ts` setting
  `startOn = createdAt` for existing rows whose `startOn` is `NULL`, and
  `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped to match `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [ ] The migration is documented in `docs/migrations/start_on.md` and
  registered so `wl doctor upgrade` lists it.
- [ ] `wl doctor` reports a mismatch where `startOn` is missing/null and
  differs from `createdAt`, with a remediation hint.
- [ ] Re-running the migration is a no-op (idempotence) and is covered by a
  test.

### Sync and export/import

- [ ] JSONL export/import round-trips `startOn`; legacy rows without the field
  import as `createdAt`.
- [ ] Two-way sync never resurrects a stale `startOn` (newest-write-wins on the
  same semantics as the other mutable fields), covered by a sync round-trip
  test.
- [ ] Cross-project dependency edges (foreign ids) are unaffected.
- [ ] `startOn` appears in every JSON surface: `show`, `list`, `search`,
  `next`, `recent`, `in_progress` and the dependency listings.

### Tests

- [ ] Unit/integration tests: default = `createdAt`; legacy JSONL import
  back-fill; sync round-trip; migration idempotence; `doctor` mismatch
  detection; all use the frozen-clock harness.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC1 — Data model.** `startOn` is stored per work item as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, exposed in every JSON surface (`show`, `list`, `search`, `next`, `recent`, `in_progress`, dependency listings). **Default = the item's `createdAt`** when omitted, including on import of legacy JSONL/Git data that has no field (back-compat is the default, never "blocked").
- [ ] **AC6 — Migration and sync.** A documented, idempotent migration sets `startOn = createdAt` for existing items (`docs/migrations/`); `doctor` reports a mismatch; JSONL export/import and Git sync round-trip the field; cross-project edges (foreign ids) are unaffected; two-way sync never resurrects a stale value.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` — `WorkItem`, `CreateWorkItemInput`, `UpdateWorkItemInput`
- `packages/shared/src/fields.ts` — `VALID_FIELDS`
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — table DDL, `SCHEMA_VERSION`, JSONL projections, index
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` — row mapping / read path
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — back-fill migration, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `src/commands/export.ts` — export projection
- `src/commands/import.ts` — legacy back-fill on import
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — mismatch check
- `src/doctor/` — check implementation
- `docs/migrations/start_on.md` — migration note

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate, frozen-clock harness and perf baseline (sibling slice 1).

## Deliverables

- Stored, indexed, always-populated `startOn` column with `createdAt` default.
- Idempotent back-fill migration + `doctor` mismatch report.
- Lossless export/import and sync round-trip.

# CLI authoring: `--start-on` on `wl create` and `wl update`

## Goal

Let operators and agents set, change and clear `startOn` from the CLI with
strict validation — the authoring half of the feature, end to end through
option parsing, normalisation, storage and `wl show` output.

## Context

The field is stored and round-tripped by the data-model slice, but nothing can
write a non-default value yet. AC2 also pins the guarantee that `wl show <id>`
is never filtered, so an item is always retrievable by id no matter its
`startOn`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `wl create --start-on <ISO-8601>` accepts a full ISO-8601 timestamp,
  **accepts a UTC offset** (`+01:00`) and normalises it to UTC `Z` form before
  storage.
- [x] `wl update <id> --start-on <ISO-8601>` behaves identically.
- [x] `--start-on ""` clears the value back to the item's `createdAt`.
- [x] An invalid value fails with an actionable message that names the flag,
  the received value and an accepted example, and the command exits non-zero
  without writing.
- [x] A bare date (`2026-11-19`) is **rejected** with the same actionable
  message (a bare date is not a date/time, and its timezone would be
  ambiguous), covered by a test. Rationale: AC2 requires invalid values to
  fail with an actionable message, and silently assuming midnight UTC would
  make a scheduling gate fire 24h early or late in some timezone.
- [x] `wl show <id>` is **never** filtered — an item is always retrievable by
  id, and the output includes `startOn`.
- [x] `wl create --help` and `wl update --help` describe the field, its
  ISO-8601 offset acceptance, the `createdAt` default and the `""` clear form.
- [x] Tests: set / clear / offset normalisation / invalid rejection / bare-date
  behaviour / `show` retrieval of a future item, all on the frozen clock.

## Impact

Operators and agents can now schedule a work item for a future instant from the CLI (`--start-on`), see it in `wl show`, and clear it back to the creation time, with ambiguous values rejected before anything is written.

### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC2 — CLI authoring.** `wl create --start-on <ISO-8601>` and `wl update <id> --start-on <ISO-8601>` (offset accepted, normalised to UTC); `--start-on ""` clears it back to `createdAt`. Invalid values fail with an actionable message. `wl show <id>` is **never** filtered — an item is always retrievable by id.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/create.ts` — `--start-on` option, normalisation, `createdAt` default
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--start-on` option, `""` clear form
- `src/argv-normalize.ts` — shared option parsing helpers (if applicable)
- `src/commands/show.ts` — confirm `startOn` in output and no filtering
- `tests/cli/create-start-on.test.ts` — option tests
- `tests/cli/update-start-on.test.ts` — option tests
- `docs/CLI.md` — flag documentation

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `startOn` data model, schema migration and sync round-trip (sibling slice 2).

## Deliverables

- Working `--start-on` on `create` and `update`, offset-normalised, validated, clearable.
- Help text and `CLI.md` coverage for the new flag.

# Default filtering across the CLI search surfaces

## Goal

Make every CLI search surface hide not-yet-started items by default, with an
explicit opt-in that still shows them — marked — in both text and JSON output.
One shared filter, applied once, so `next`, `worklist` and Herdr cannot diverge.

## Impact

Operators no longer see work that cannot be started yet: scheduled items stay out of `list`/`search`/`next`/`recent`/`worklist` until their start time, and `--include-not-started` brings them back clearly marked instead of silently.

## Context

The choke point is `src/worklist-selection.ts` (`selectBrowseFeed`), which
`wl next`, `wl worklist` and the Herdr fetchers all go through. The filter
belongs there plus the per-command read paths, never forked per command
(intake note on the parent item). `in_progress` items are never filtered out —
a started item has already started.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Default exclusion

- [ ] `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the
  equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future.
- [ ] `wl worklist` (the consolidated `db.list()` + shared browse-feed read)
  applies the same default filter to every subset.
- [ ] The shared browse-feed selection (`src/worklist-selection.ts`) carries
  the filter so `next`, `worklist` and the Herdr fetchers agree by construction.
- [ ] `in_progress` items are never filtered out, even if their `startOn` is in
  the future (`wl in_progress` and the `in_progress` subset of `worklist`).
- [ ] `wl show <id>` remains unfiltered.

### Opt-in

- [ ] An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before
  <ISO>`) shows not-yet-started items on every surface listed above.
- [ ] Opted-in items are marked as not yet started in **both** text and JSON
  output. Text carries a trailing marker in the same bracketed style the
  worklist already uses for `[held: N by Map]`:
  `[not started until 2026-11-19T10:25:00Z]` (effective `startOn`, UTC `Z`
  form). JSON carries `notStarted: true` alongside the effective `startOn`.
- [ ] `--include-not-started` and `--starts-before <ISO>` compose: with both,
  the window is "not started AND starting before `<ISO>`".
- [ ] The filter is clock-injectable through the shared predicate so tests use
  a frozen clock.

### Tests

- [ ] Tests prove a future item is excluded from each surface in the list
  above, included with the opt-in, and correctly marked in text and JSON.
- [ ] A test proves an `in_progress` item with a future `startOn` still appears.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC3 — Default filtering in searches.** `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent` and the equivalent JSON paths **exclude** items whose `startOn` is in the future. An explicit opt-in (`--include-not-started`, and/or `--starts-before <ISO>`) shows them, marked as not yet started in both text and JSON output. `in_progress` items are never filtered out (a started item has already started).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/list.ts` — default exclusion + opt-in flags
- `src/commands/search.ts` — same default exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/next.ts` — browse-feed selection
- `src/commands/in-progress.ts` — exclusion, never filtering in-progress items
- `src/commands/recent.ts` — exclusion + opt-in
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — consolidated read, same filter for every subset
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — shared browse-feed filter (single choke point)
- `packages/shared/src/database/next-pipeline.ts` — selection query
- `src/cli-output.ts` — the not-yet-started marker in text/JSON output
- `docs/CLI.md` — `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before`

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate slice (1).
- Depends on: `startOn` data model slice (2).
- Depends on: CLI authoring slice (3) — integration tests author future items with `--start-on`.

## Deliverables

- Default exclusion of not-yet-started items on all six CLI search surfaces.
- `--include-not-started` / `--starts-before` opt-in with a text and JSON marker.
- Shared browse-feed filter that Herdr inherits.
data.title: Filter not-yet-started items by default across CLI search surfaces

# Claim guard: refuse a future claim with an audited override

## Goal

Make it structurally impossible to claim work that has not started yet —
while keeping a deliberate, audited escape hatch for an operator who needs to
start early.

## Context

Defence in depth: the default filter (slice 4) hides future items, but a direct
`wl update <id> --status in_progress` or an explicit id-targeted claim must
still be refused. The refusal must be machine-readable so Herdr and skill
scripts can branch on it rather than parse prose. `src/claim-hold.ts` and
`src/claim-hold-read.ts` host the existing claim-path surfaces; the Herdr claim
path is `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.claim.ts` / `index.claim.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Setting an item to `in_progress` (or any claim path, including the Herdr
  claim and the `StatusLifecycle` claim helper) on a future `startOn` is
  **refused** with the machine-readable reason `start_on_not_reached` in JSON
  output, and a non-zero exit.
- [ ] The refusal message names the item's effective `startOn` and how long
  until it is reached.
- [ ] An explicit, auditable override is available (proposed flag:
  `--force-start-on <reason>`; the implementer may rename it if the CLI
  convention demands) — when passed, the claim proceeds **and** a comment is
  written naming the actor, the reason and the `startOn` that was overridden.
- [ ] The override comment is visible in `wl show <id>` comments and survives
  export/import.
- [ ] The guard must **not** fire for `createdAt`-defaulted items, nor for any
  item whose effective `startOn` is at or before `now`.
- [ ] The guard composes with the existing gates — it never replaces the
  `assignee` hold, dependency readiness or `needsProducerReview`, and is an
  additional sequential refusal.
- [ ] Tests: claim refused; claim allowed after the instant (frozen clock);
  override succeeds and writes the audited comment; `createdAt`-defaulted items
  never refused.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC5 — Claim guard (defence in depth).** Setting an item to `in_progress` (or any claim path) on a future `startOn` is refused with a machine-readable reason (`start_on_not_reached`) unless an explicit, auditable override is passed; the override writes a comment naming the actor and the reason. The guard must not fire for `createdAt`-defaulted items.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — the `--status in_progress` transition and the override flag
- `src/claim-hold.ts` — claim-path policy surface
- `src/claim-hold-read.ts` — claim-path read surface
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.claim.ts` — Herdr claim path
- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — Herdr claim wiring
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — dispatch-side refusal token
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — `ClassifyGateToken` union
- `docs/CLI.md` — refusal reason and override flag

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate slice (1).
- Depends on: `startOn` data model slice (2).
- Depends on: CLI authoring slice (3) — tests author future items with `--start-on`.

## Deliverables

- `start_on_not_reached` refusal across every claim path.
- Audited override that records actor, reason and the overridden instant.

## Impact

Users can now safely schedule work items for a future date and be certain that no agent, dispatcher or session will claim them before that instant — while a deliberate early start remains possible through an audited override that permanently records who did it, why, and which startOn they bypassed.
data.title: Refuse future claims with an audited start_on_not_reached override

# Herdr parity: dispatch gate and read-only worklist marker

## Goal

Guarantee a not-yet-started item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr
worker, while the operator can still *see* it in the worklist with a
"not started until <date>" marker — read-only, never altered.

## Context

Herdr has two distinct paths: the *queries* it issues through `wl` (and the
`fetcher*` family), and its own local dispatch pipeline
(`downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` → `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` in
`downtime-worker.gates.ts`). Parity requires both. The read-only banner
convention is `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts`
(WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR): derived from items the worklist has *already* fetched,
no extra `wl` spawn, no mutation, no second ranking path. Mirror it.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Never dispatch a future item

- [ ] Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default
  filter as the CLI, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any
  Herdr worker.
- [ ] A dedicated `startOnNotReached` gate is added to
  `classifyItemForDispatchDetail` (as a new `ClassifyGateToken` member) and
  refuses at **every** tier (intake, plan, risk-effort, implement, audit).
- [ ] The Herdr list-head dispatch pipeline
  (`downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`) filters not-yet-started items out of
  its candidate set.
- [ ] The gate is clock-injectable and covered by a frozen-clock test proving
  no tier can select a future item.

### Read-only visibility

- [ ] Not-yet-started items are surfaced **read-only** in the worklist with a
  "not started until <date>" marker.
- [ ] The marker follows the existing held-items banner convention
  (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR): a header count plus a banner, derived from the
  already-fetched window, with no additional `wl` subprocess and no second
  ranking path. Concretely, mirroring `assigneeHoldStatusText` /
  `assigneeHoldBannerText`:
  - header indicator `[not started: N]`, `null` when N is 0 (no chrome for the
    common case);
  - banner `Not started — all N of M dispatch-window item(s) start after
    <earliest startOn>; no downtime dispatch possible`, rendered only when the
    whole window is not-yet-started.
- [ ] A per-row marker `[not started until <date>]` distinguishes individual
  not-yet-started rows from already-started ones.
- [ ] The surface never clears or alters the item's state — no claim, no
  status/stage write, no `startOn` change (strictly read-only, mirroring
  `dispatch-window-hold.ts` AC4).
- [ ] Existing held-items semantics are unchanged: a held item is still
  reported by the hold banner, and an item that is both held and not started
  does not double-count in a way that misreports either bucket.
- [ ] Tests: the marker renders for a future item; the banner appears when the
  whole window is not-yet-started; no mutation is performed.


### Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim)

These restate the covering parent acceptance criteria word for word so
the parent/child AC-coverage check is exact.

- [ ] **AC4 — Herdr plugin parity.** Worklist, dispatcher and audit-pickup queries apply the same default filter, so a future item is never dispatched or claimed by any Herdr worker. Surface not-yet-started items **read-only** in the worklist with a "not started until <date>" marker, following the existing held-items banner convention (WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR), and never clear or alter their state.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — surface the marker
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatch-window-hold.ts` — reference banner implementation
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.detail.ts` — detail rendering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.meta.ts` — header counts
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` — list-head dispatch pipeline
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `startOnNotReached` gate
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — `ClassifyGateToken`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — CLI-backed query path
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` — in-process query path
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher behaviour

## Dependencies

- Depends on: `isNotStarted` predicate slice (1).
- Depends on: `startOn` data model slice (2).
- Depends on: CLI default-filtering slice (4) — Herdr inherits the shared browse-feed filter.

## Deliverables

- `startOnNotReached` dispatch gate at every tier.
- Filtered Herdr queries and list-head pipeline.
- Read-only "not started until" marker and banner in the worklist.

## Impact

A Herdr operator can now see scheduled-but-not-yet-started work items in the worklist with an explicit "not started until <date>" per-row marker, header count and all-scheduled banner, while no dispatcher or audit pickup can start them early.
data.title: Add Herdr parity: startOn dispatch gate and read-only worklist marker

# Placement gate false-positive blocks epic driving on a busy machine

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent <epic>` refuses to proceed for an epic child whose
worktree exists but holds no changes whenever **any** other registered
worktree of the repository is dirty:

```
ERROR: Child WL-... produced changes in the sibling worktree
.../worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC... instead of its worktree ...
Offending paths: ...
```

`_child_main_checkout_violation` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`)
treats "child worktree clean + sibling worktree dirty" as evidence that the
child wrote outside its tree. Condition 3 of its documented precision rule
says pre-existing/unrelated dirt must not block a legitimate child, but the
code only earns that exemption when the child's own worktree already holds
changes — which a **freshly started child never does**. The result: on a
machine running several concurrent dispatches (the normal steady state),
`parent` and `drive` fail closed before the first child session is ever
spawned.

## Evidence (captured 2026-11-18, parent epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9)

1. `implement.py parent WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` started child
   WL-0MWKY141H002LULI and created its (empty) worktree.
2. `implement.py drive WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` then failed in `phase_parent`
   with one message per dirty sibling worktree:
   - `wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG-...` (item soft-deleted, 3 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MVOBP8MC0093Y7T-...` (blocked item, 22 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV-...` (live concurrent dispatch, 15 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWMGEL5R003IH71-...` (6 dirty paths)
   - `/tmp/wl-base-check`, `/tmp/wl-clean-check`, ... (1 dirty path each)
   `sessions_spawned: 0` — no child session ran, so no child work existed.
3. Removing the empty worktree (`implement.py abort`) and re-running `drive`
   let the chain start normally: `phase_start` recreated the tree and the
   session was spawned, precisely because no clean worktree existed at the
   moment the placement check ran.

## Desired change

A freshly started child (worktree created, no session spawned against it yet)
must never be reported as a placement violation because of dirt in a
*different* work item's worktree. Candidate treatments, in order of
preference:

- Exempt a child whose worktree was created by this run's `phase_start` and
  has never had a session spawned against it (the same shape as the existing
  `read_spawn_failure` exemption).
- Restrict the sibling scan to worktrees whose dirt this child's session could

## Goal

Encode the new priority-band ordering contract as executable tests **before** any production code changes, so the two implementation items work against a red specification rather than a guess.

## Scope

Tests only — **no production source is edited in this item**. `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, `src/commands/grouping.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` must be untouched (the diff for this item is test files only).

Tests are added to:

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — herdr `assignItemGroups` / `compareGroupableItems`
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — the core mirror used by `wl next --groups`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts` — selection truncation

## Contract under test

- **Band order:** `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review` (single global section, pinned last).
- **Intra-band stage sub-order:** `status='in-progress'` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other. Stage never reorders across bands.
- **The inversion case:** a `high@idea` item's group number is lower than every `medium@plan_complete` item's group number (today the stage bucket wins and the medium renders above the high).
- **Per-band file-path grouping:** greedy first-fit inside each band, at most 3 file-path groups per band-section, two same-band items sharing a Key File never share a group, items with no Key Files stay singleton groups.
- **`In Review` pin:** rendered as the final section regardless of the priority of its members.
- **Selection truncation:** with 5 high and 2 medium non-mandatory items and `othersLimit = 3`, all three selected `others` are high — no medium displaces a high.
- **Mandatory guarantee unchanged:** every `critical`, `status='in-progress'`, `status='blocked'` and `in_review`+`completed` item is selected regardless of the window.
- **Purity:** the same item set in any arrival order / `updatedAt` order groups identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each contract bullet above has at least one named test in the files listed under Scope, with an assertion message that identifies the specific inversion or ordering rule being violated.
- The new tests fail against current `main` sources for the expected reason (red for the inversion/selection cases, not for compile or fixture errors) when run through the test skill (`/skill:test`).
- Tests that encode ordering unchanged by this work (in_review bucket sort, expand reachability, mandatory always-show) remain green and are left semantically untouched.
- At least one test exercises the **core** copy (`src/commands/grouping.ts`) for the band order, not only the herdr copy, so the mirror is specified too.
- The selection test asserts both the selected set **and** that the incoming score order is preserved within a priority band (the score tie-break must come from `wl next` order, not a re-sort).
- No ad-hoc test command is used; the red/green evidence comes from the test skill.

- New tests cover the high@idea vs medium@plan_complete inversion (both copies), the `In Review` pin, per-band file-path grouping, and the selection-truncation case; existing grouping/selection tests are updated rather than deleted.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`

## Notes

Test-first ordering: this item must land before the two grouping implementation items and before the selection item. Fixtures should be shared helpers inside each test file (no new production helper) to keep the diff test-only.

## Impact

Producers browsing the sprint view and running `wl next --groups` get priority-first ordering (high above medium above low, regardless of stage), pinned by executable contract tests so a later change cannot silently sink a high-priority item below a medium one.

## Goal

Rewrite `assignItemGroups` in the herdr plugin so sections are bucketed by **priority band first**, with stage used only as the intra-band sub-order — a `high@idea` item can then never render below a `medium@plan_complete` item.

## Implementation

1. Replace the stage-derived bucket assembly (`Critical Group N` → `Group N` → `Idea` → `Other` → `In Review`) with a band loop over `['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low']`.
2. Inside each band:
   - `critical` keeps today's file-path partitioning (`Critical Group N`, per-category label counter).
   - Non-critical bands partition the band's actively-worked / `plan_complete` / `intake_complete` items by file-path conflicts (`<Band> Group N`), then emit a single `<Band> Idea` group and a single `<Band> Other` group for the band.
   - `maxFilePathGroups` (default 3) applies **per band-section**; the label counter restarts at 1 per band.
3. Extend `WITHIN_GROUP_STAGE_ORDER` with `idea: 3` and raise `REMAINING_STAGE_ORDER` to 4, so `compareGroupableItems` and `compareGroupingContentKey` express `in-progress → plan_complete → intake_complete → idea → other`.
4. Keep `compareGroupableItems` (priority-first), `canonicalizeForGrouping`, `groupItemsByFilePaths`, `buildLabelCounter`, `remapToSequential` and the `in_review` bucket sort semantically unchanged — only bucket assembly and the stage-order table change.
5. Emit `In Review` last as one global section, never inside a band.
6. Update the module header group-order documentation and keep the "mirrors `src/commands/grouping.ts`" note accurate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `high@idea` sits in a lower-numbered group than every `medium@plan_complete` item for a mixed fixture; the inversion test from the contract-tests item passes.
- Section order is `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `In Review` independent of stage; a low-priority `plan_complete` item never outranks a high-priority `idea` item.
- Intra-band stage sub-order is `in-progress` → `plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → `idea` → other, and stage never reorders across bands.
- `In Review` is a single final section regardless of the priority of its members.
- Labels are `Critical Group N`, `High Group N`, `Medium Group N`, `Low Group N`, `<Band> Idea`, `<Band> Other`, `In Review`; label counters restart per band.
- Per-band file-path grouping holds: two same-band items sharing a Key File never share a group, at most 3 file-path groups per band-section, no-Key-Files items are singleton groups.
- Grouping stays a pure function of item content — no dependence on `updatedAt`, arrival order or pin-map insertion order (permutation test).
- The herdr grouping test suite is green through the test skill; no other production module is modified.

- A mixed set of `high@idea` and `medium@plan_complete` items is regrouped so every high item's group number is lower than every medium item's — the inversion is gone.
- Section labels follow the band scheme: `Critical Group N`, `High Group N`, `Medium Group N`, `Low Group N`; no non-critical section is labelled plain `Group N`.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`

## Notes

`packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`computeScore`) is explicitly out of scope. The core `wl next --groups` copy is a separate item; this item changes herdr only, and the module header must still state the two copies are kept in sync.

## Impact

Producers see every high-priority item above every medium-priority item in the herdr sprint view regardless of lifecycle stage, so urgent ideas are no longer buried beneath less urgent planned work.

## Goal

Order the non-mandatory `others` slice priority-first **before** the `othersLimit` truncation so a medium-priority item can never displace a high-priority one from the sprint window.

## Implementation

1. In `selectWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`), sort the `others` slice with a **stable** comparator on priority band (`high` → `medium` → `low`; unknown → `medium`) immediately before `.slice(0, othersLimit)`.
2. The incoming `wl next` score order is the intra-band tie-break: a stable priority sort preserves it. Do **not** re-score — `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`computeScore`) is untouched by this item and by the parent.
3. Keep mandatory-set assembly unchanged (criticals, `in_review`+`completed`, `status='blocked'`, `status='in-progress'`), including the root-only filter and the `done` exclusion.
4. Document the ordering and the stable-sort/sub-score relationship in the module header.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With 5 high and 2 medium non-mandatory items and `othersLimit = 3`, all three selected `others` are high-priority — no medium displaces a high.
- With `othersLimit` larger than the high count, the remaining slots are filled with mediums in their incoming score order (stable sort, rank order preserved within a band).
- The mandatory always-show guarantee is unchanged: every `critical`, `status='in-progress'`, `status='blocked'` and `in_review`+`completed` item is still selected regardless of the window, and mandatory items never consume a slice they previously did not.
- `selectWorkItems` remains pure and deterministic: no input mutation, same input → same output.
- Existing smart-selection tests are updated to the new contract and all pass through the test skill.
- A test asserts the reproduced anomaly is gone: a fresh audit-not-ready medium (score 5500) no longer out-selects a plain high (score 3000).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`

## Notes

Whether `others` already arrive score-ordered from `wl next` is asserted by a test (incoming order within a band must be preserved) rather than assumed; if the fetcher does not guarantee score order, document that in the module header and keep the stable sort as the guarantee boundary.

## Impact

A producer browsing the sprint view now sees high-priority work in the selection window even when fresh-audit medium items outrank it by score, so the most urgent work can no longer be silently cut.

data.description:
## Goal

Prove that the blocker-pin override and the critical-root substitution keep working under the band-first structure, so the mandatory/pin guarantees are not silently regressed by the re-bucketing.

## Implementation

1. Pin tests (WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC): a pinned blocker is grouped **with** the item it blocks — same band section and group number — and sorts immediately after it; multi-block first-group-wins still yields exactly one row; an absent or empty pin map leaves the output byte-identical to the unpinned grouping.
2. Root substitution: a substituted critical root is grouped by **its own priority band** (it is not marked critical), keeps `childCount > 0` so the expand affordance survives, and is not duplicated when already present.
3. Check the selection tail in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`: if it derives or re-numbers group headings, the band-first numbering must survive; fix any assumption that a section number identifies a stage bucket.
4. Add the missing regression tests where coverage is absent; do not weaken existing pin/substitution tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pinned blocker shares its blocked item's `group` and `groupLabel` inside the blocked item's priority band and sorts immediately after it.
- A blocker blocking two visible items in two different bands appears exactly once, in the lowest-numbered group in display order.
- An empty or absent pin map produces output identical to the unpinned band-first grouping.
- A substituted critical root appears once, grouped by its own band, with `childCount` preserved.
- `fetcher.root-substitution.ts` contains no stage-bucket assumption; if one was found, it is corrected and covered by a test.
- The related regression tests pass through the test skill together with the grouping and selection suites.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (pin override path — read/verify, change only if a genuine band assumption is found)
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`

## Related work

- `WL-0MW7YJYS5009H7WC` — blocker pinning (group override that must be preserved).
- `WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB` / `WL-0MV6KV22S004NYIU` / `WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE` — mandatory always-show guarantees.

## Impact

Operators can trust that a blocked row is still paired with the work that unblocks it and that a critical child's root still appears in its own priority band, so the band-first layout cannot silently hide the dependency or the release-blocking work.

# Validate post-fix dispatch fairness after three days

Earliest run: **2026-11-22T15:30:00Z** (three days after the operator restarted
the downtime dispatcher panes on 2026-11-19T~15:15Z). Until that instant there
is no post-fix window long enough to judge, so this item is scheduled with
`startOn` rather than being dispatched immediately.

Follow-up from **WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K** (the post-fix re-measurement, which was
reported *inconclusive* because the live dispatcher was still running pre-fix
code) and from parent **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** AC5.

## Why

The fairness fix (whole-set round-robin rotation + `RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2`,
commits `ef46c0bd8` / `7a0d1460c`) is now live: the operator restarted every
Herdr `Work Items` plugin pane, so the dispatcher loads current
`packages/herdr/src`. The only remaining question is whether the live
behaviour actually meets the thresholds over a real window — which needs
elapsed time, not code.

## Users

The operator of the multi-project Herdr workspace (single user, 10 registered
project roots), who relies on the downtime dispatcher to spread agent sessions
evenly instead of letting one project monopolise the slots.

- As the workspace operator, I want a measured pass/fail on the fairness rule
  over a real post-restart window, so that "the fix works" is evidence rather
  than assumption.
- As the workspace operator, I want the measurement reproducible from the logs
  alone, so that a future reader can re-derive it after the logs have rotated.

## Scope

Read-only validation. No code change is expected; if the numbers fail, record
the evidence and file a follow-up work item rather than editing the dispatcher
from this item.

- Confirm from `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` that decision entries now
  carry the fairness metric (`selectedRoot`, and `dispatchingRoot` +
  `consecutiveRunLength` on consumed dispatches) — proof the current code is
  live.
- Measure the window from each project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`
  (rows with a `paneId`) using the counting rules recorded in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Cross-check the dispatch-log distribution against the decision-log fairness
  metric (the accounting identity).
- Report the result on **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**.

## Existing state

Captured at intake (2026-11-19T23:35Z) — indicative only; it is **not** the
measurement this item asks for, and the measured window must still be taken
after 2026-11-22T15:30Z.

- **The regime check already passes by observation.** Fairness-bearing decision
  entries (`selectedRoot`) first appear at `2026-11-19T18:01:53.039Z`
  (`projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) and, in the
  downtime leader's own log, from `2026-11-19T20:47:02.017Z`
  (`projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) — both after the
  ~15:15Z restart, so the running code includes the fairness accounting. AC1
  should be re-confirmed against the measured window, not assumed from this.
- The leader's log is where decisions land: 17 fairness-bearing decision rows
  between `2026-11-19T20:47:02Z` and `2026-11-19T23:34:39Z` — 14
  `reason: "dispatched"`, 3 `reason: "reservation-refused"`. Distinct
  `selectedRoot`s: SorraAgents 5, ContextHub 5, AI_Hell 3, tce-the-rising 2,
  games_curator 2 (5 active projects ≥ the three-project floor).
- Every recorded `consecutiveRunLength` in that leader-log window is `1`; the
  only `2` observed today is `2026-11-19T18:17:34.785Z` in
  `projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`. 14 dispatches is
  far too small a sample to declare anything.
- **Open point for the measurement:** 2 of the 17 rows record `selectedRoot`
  ≠ `dispatchingRoot` (`18:01:53Z` and `23:18:07Z`). The counting rules charge
  `dispatchingRoot`, so this is either a benign deferral/ordering effect or a
  real accounting-identity mismatch — the AC4 cross-check is where it gets
  settled, and the finding must be stated either way.
- The round-robin cursor file (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`)
  currently lists 10 roots; the recent window served 5 of them.

## Data sources (read-only)

- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` — per project; the leader's copy carries
  the decision rows (periodically rotated, ~500 lines).
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — per project; dispatch rows carrying a
  `paneId` (rotated, ~500 lines per project — evidence disappears within
  hours, so capture aggregates as soon as they are read).
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` — cursor state at the
  window boundary.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the counting rules ("*Counting rules.*"
  section: window, rows, project key, regime check, even share, consecutive
  run, kind mix, accounting identity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision entry carrying `selectedRoot` is observed after the restart
  timestamp, confirming the current code is live.
- A window with at least three active projects is measured, stating the window
  (UTC start/end), the project count and the counting rules used.
- No project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches in that window, and no
  project holds a consecutive run longer than 2.
- The distribution derived from the decision-log fairness metric agrees with
  the dispatch-log aggregates for the same window.
- The table (per-project counts, longest consecutive runs, kind mix) and an
  explicit pass/fail against both thresholds are reported on
  WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9; a fail records the evidence, the suspected cause and a
  follow-up work item.
- If the window has fewer than three active projects, the measurement is
  recorded as inconclusive (with the extended window or the reason it could
  not be extended) rather than declared a pass.
- The captured aggregates and the exact read-only commands/queries used are
  recorded on this work item (not only in the report comment), so the result
  can be re-derived after the logs rotate.
- Any documentation claim that the measurement contradicts (e.g. in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) is corrected; if that — or a follow-up fix
  arising from a fail — produces a code or doc change, the full project test
  suite must pass with that change.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no dispatcher behaviour change, no gate change, no scheduler
  change.
- Measure only after the restart marker is visible — a window spanning the
  restart would mix two code versions.
- Log rotation (500 lines per project) discards evidence within hours: capture
  the aggregates as soon as they are read and record them on the item.
- Report on a completed parent (**WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**, `completed`/`in_review`)
  via a comment; do not reopen it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Small sample.** Rotation keeps ~500 lines per project and the recent rate is
  ~14 dispatches in 3 hours, so a three-day window may still be a thin sample;
  state the dispatch total and do not declare a pass on a handful of rows.
- **Too few active projects.** Overnight/weekend windows can drop below three
  active projects; AC6 already requires recording *inconclusive* rather than a
  pass.
- **Mixed regime.** Any window reaching back past `2026-11-19T18:01Z` mixes the
  pre-fix worker's rows; the window must start after the restart marker.
- **Assumption:** the leader's `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (currently
  SorraAgents) is the canonical decision log; per-project logs receive only the
  rows that project's pane produced.
- **Assumption:** `dispatchingRoot` is the charged root (the counting rules say
  so), so the two observed `selectedRoot` ≠ `dispatchingRoot` rows are explained
  by deferral/ordering rather than by a defect — AC4 must prove it.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A failing measurement invites an immediate dispatcher
  fix; that is deliberately out of scope here (read-only), so any fix becomes a
  new linked work item with its own ACs and release gate.

## Impact

The operator gets a measured, reproducible verdict on whether the dispatcher's
fixed fair-sharing actually holds live, so even distribution across their
projects is evidenced rather than assumed.

**Key Files:**

- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (per project; read-only) — decision rows; regime check (`selectedRoot`) and accounting identity (`dispatchingRoot`, `consecutiveRunLength`)
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (per project; read-only) — dispatch rows with a `paneId`; per-project counts, runs, kind mix
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` — cursor state at the window boundary
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — counting rules and thresholds to quote with the result
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — where the fairness fields are written (reference only; no change expected)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-entries.ts` — dispatch-row shape (`paneId`, `cwd`, `kind`)

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** — *Dispatcher seems to unevenly distribute work*
  (completed/in_review) — the epic; AC5 is this validation, and the report goes
  here.
- **WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K** — *Re-measure dispatch concentration after the fix*
  (completed/in_review) — the first attempt; reported *inconclusive* because
  the live worker still ran pre-fix code. Its counting methodology and outcome
  section are the template for this item.
- **WL-0MWKY141H002LULI** — *Record per-project fairness metric on dispatch
  decisions* (completed) — added the `selectedRoot`/`dispatchingRoot`/
  `consecutiveRunLength` fields this measurement reads.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** — *Docs: the enforced fair-scheduling rule and its
  metric* (completed) — the counting rules and metric documentation.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** — *Rotate the whole admissible candidate set with a
  run-length bound* (completed) — the fix under test (`RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2`).
- **WL-0MWO38U4W002853V** — *Publish fairness report and update documentation*
  (blocked/intake_complete) — downstream consumer of a passing result; blocked,
  so it cannot absorb this measurement.
- Repo docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — "Re-measuring concentration
  after a fix" / *Counting rules*.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No interview questions were asked.** The item had been re-scoped by a prior
  `implement` session and already carried a problem statement, scope, six
  testable acceptance criteria, data sources and constraints, so the interview
  was skipped per the intake contract (seed context sufficient to draft).
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of the completed re-measurement (WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K)?**
  — Answer (agent research, source: `wl show WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K --json`): No.
  That item closed *inconclusive* because the live dispatcher still ran pre-fix
  code; its ACs were therefore not satisfied by observation. This item measures
  a fresh window after the operator's restart, which is the gap it leaves.
  Partial overlap only — no rewrite needed; the description already isolates the
  post-restart window.
- **Q: Is `chore` the right issue type?** — Answer (agent decision): yes — no
  code behaviour changes; this is operational validation plus reporting, with a
  conditional doc correction only on a contradictory finding.
- **Q: Why was the automated `/skill:find-related` report not generated?** —
  Answer (agent research): the script re-claims the item with
  `--status in-progress`, which the `startOn` claim guard
  (`src/claim-start-on.ts`, WL-0MWMGEUT10056MUI) refuses with
  `start_on_not_reached` until 2026-11-22T15:30Z, and it exposes no
  `--force-start-on` passthrough. The `## Related work` list above was therefore
  gathered manually from `wl search` / `wl list --parent` and is idempotent to
  re-run later.

# Fairness across remote dispatching hosts

Investigation item: **examine why one machine obtains a disproportionate share
of the shared dispatch slots when several hosts dispatch at once, and present
potential solutions.** The deliverable is an evidence-backed RCA plus an options
paper with one recommendation — implementation is deferred to follow-up items
(including a cross-repo proxy item where required).

## Problem statement

When more than one host runs downtime dispatchers against the same shared
llama-proxy, one machine consistently holds an unfair share of the scarce local
GPU slots: its panes occupy slot time while other hosts' dispatchable work waits
or is never dispatched. The suspicion is that the winning host is simply the one
running more dispatcher instances / agent panes, because slot arbitration is
keyed to the **session**, not to the **host** — so a host's share grows with the
number of sessions it happens to have live.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle capacity shared across hosts on a rule I can
  state and verify, so that a machine running many dispatchers does not
  monopolise the GPU slot budget at the expense of a machine running one.
- **As a project owner whose work sits on a starved host**, I want to see from
  the logs *why* my host got no slot (host-share, lease retention, budget, or a
  safety gate) rather than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness invariant enforced (or
  at least measured and documented) by the code path that actually grants a
  slot, with a way to detect regression from the recorded evidence.
- **As the proxy maintainer**, I want any host-aware arbitration to reuse the
  existing lease/queue machinery and the existing client-identity logging,
  without adding a second scheduler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A per-host measurement is recorded on this work item: for one documented
  window with at least two participating hosts, a table of, per host,
  dispatched-pane count, local slot-seconds held, active vs. retained (idle)
  lease time and share of total; the data sources (proxy structured logs with
  `client_ip`, per-host downtime dispatch logs, lease events) and the exact
  queries used are documented so an auditor can reproduce the table.
- A root-cause analysis names every mechanism that can push a host's share above
  a fair share, with code references and evidence, or rules it out with
  evidence. At minimum evaluate: (a) session-keyed lease acquisition with
  same-session re-acquisition and non-preemptive idle-lease retention; (b) a
  host's share scaling with its number of dispatcher instances / live panes;
  (c) the free-slot gate reading one global slot snapshot, so the earliest or
  fastest poller wins; (d) the absence of any host-keyed slot accounting today.
- A definition of "fair" is documented and justified, stating explicitly how it
  treats hosts with **different numbers of dispatcher instances** (the
  invariant to hold: a host's share must not scale with its instance count) and
  hosts with different capacity, plus what happens when a host has no
  dispatchable work.
- At least two candidate solutions are presented with trade-offs, each naming
  the component it changes (herdr dispatcher vs. llama-proxy), its failure
  modes, its fail-open behaviour, and whether it needs a cross-repo proxy change
  (a new `LP-` work item) or can be done dispatcher-side; the options must
  include at least one that works without a proxy change.
- One recommendation is made — the smallest change that makes host share
  independent of instance count — with its residual risks and the follow-up
  work items required to implement it recorded and linked (this item does not
  implement it).
- Validation: every quantitative claim in the report is reproducible from a
  documented command or query on a named host; any helper script added for the
  measurement has a unit test covering its reduction logic.
- Fairness cannot regress the existing dispatch gates: critical-first,
  review-queue depth, code-freeze, host-CPU gate, host dispatch budget and the
  audit tier must be shown to behave exactly as today (by inspection of the
  proposed change surface, since this item ships no behaviour change).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The operator can see, host by host, how shared dispatch capacity is actually
distributed and why one machine dominates — and gets a single change that makes
each host's share depend on the work it has, not on how many dispatchers happen
to be running there.

## Constraints

- **Investigation, not a scheduler rewrite.** Deliver measured evidence, a
  fairness definition, options and one recommendation. Record implementation as
  follow-up items rather than doing it here.
- **Cross-repo boundary.** Proxy arbitration lives in `llm-manager` (`LP-`
  prefix, e.g. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`); herdr-side work must not assume a
  new proxy contract exists. Any host-aware arbitration that must run in the
  proxy needs its own `LP-` work item and a version-tolerant client.
- **Fail-open.** Any new accounting or arbitration must never refuse a dispatch
  because a read, lock or log parse failed; a failure degrades to today's
  behaviour.
- **Hot-path budget.** No additional `wl` spawn per tick; measurement runs
  off-log, not in the dispatch loop.
- **Gates preserved.** Critical-first, review-queue, code-freeze, host-CPU gate,
  host dispatch budget and audit admission keep their current precedence;
  fairness never buys itself by relaxing a safety gate.
- **No unilateral cap changes.** Changing per-host `budget.json` defaults
  (`maxImplement: 2`, `maxAudit: 1`) or the proxy's `session_slot_pool_size` is
  a producer decision; the options paper must quantify such a change rather than
  apply it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: wrong resource.** If "slots" turns out not to be the proxy's local
  slots, the measurement AC still surfaces the real contention point (AC1
  requires both slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host); the options
  paper must then address whatever the data shows.
- **Risk: measurement needs a quiet or attributable window.** Proxy logs carry
  `client_ip`, but a `local-preferred` request routed to a remote provider never
  holds a local slot, so slot-seconds and dispatch counts must be reported
  separately to avoid a misleading ratio.
- **Risk: proxy change is a separate release train.** A host-aware lease needs
  an `LP-` item and a version-tolerant herdr client; the dispatcher-side option
  is the fallback if the proxy change stalls.
- **Risk: fairness versus throughput.** Per-host caps can idle the GPU when one
  host has all the work; the options paper must quantify the idle cost of each
  option rather than trading throughput silently.
- **Scope-creep guard:** fixing per-host fairness in code, changing
  `budget.json` defaults, changing `session_slot_pool_size`, or building a
  dashboard is **out of scope** — record each as a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A1–A4** are recorded in the appendix and need producer
  confirmation at review; none blocks starting the investigation.

## Existing state

- **Dispatch-side fairness is per machine, by construction.** The coordination
  dir, leader election and dispatch-budget ledger are single-machine
  (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, `machine-coordination.ts`); the docs state the local
  coordination/ledger paths are single-machine and that only the audit budget is
  cross-machine, via the proxy. Per-host caps today are `maxImplement: 2` /
  legacy `maxAudit: 1` in `budget.json`.
- **The genuinely shared resource across hosts is the proxy's local slots.** The
  dispatcher's free-slot gate reads one **global** slot snapshot from
  `GET {proxyUrl}/llama/local/status`; whoever polls and dispatches first takes
  the slot.
- **Slot arbitration is session-keyed, not host-keyed.**
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch(srv, max_local, session_key, …)` admits up to
  `session_slot_pool_size` concurrent sessions; same-session re-acquisition is
  always permitted, and the no-preemption policy lets an inactive (post-request
  cooldown) lease keep reserving its slot for the owning session. Nothing in the
  lease record names the host.
- **Host attribution exists only in logs.** The proxy resolves and logs
  `client_ip` / `client_ip_source` / `client_port` on status and lease events
  (LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88), so per-host slot-seconds are measurable after the fact,
  but no arbitration or accounting path consumes host identity.
- **Per-project rotation already exists and is single-machine.** The
  least-recently-served root ordering with a twice-in-succession run-length
  bound (`downtime-worker.fairness.ts`, WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 /
  WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O) fixes *project* concentration on one host; it has no
  notion of a host and cannot arbitrate across machines.
- **Prior attribution incident.** A 2026-08 investigation (WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T)
  found ~8 un-attributable `status_request` pollers, 3–4 concurrent connections
  from a single remote host; client-IP logging was added as the fix. That is the
  precedent for measuring rather than guessing.

## Desired change

A published report (e.g. `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md`, linked from
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) containing: the per-host share measurement
and its methodology, the fairness definition and invariant, the root-cause
findings with code references, the candidate solutions with trade-offs and a
recommendation, and links to the follow-up implementation items. No behaviour
change in this item.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md` — new report: measurement, fairness definition, root causes, options, recommendation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — cross-host fairness section/link; correct any "single-machine only" wording that measurement contradicts
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-cpu-gate.ts` — global free-slot gate (candidate dispatcher-side lever); inspect for the host-count interaction, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — per-host ledger/caps (`maxImplement`, `maxAudit`) referenced by the options paper, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — machine-scope contract and its doc comment (any wording change)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — existing per-host observability surface, candidate place to surface host share
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness.ts` — per-project rotation (contrast: why it cannot arbitrate across hosts)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` session-keyed leases (proxy-side option; cross-repo `LP-` item)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `_resolve_client_ip` / `_resolve_client_id`, the host-attribution seam used for measurement
- `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — existing fairness discussion (per-session FIFO), the design context for any proxy-side option

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (completed) — dispatcher unevenly distributes work
  across *projects* on one machine; measured the same class of concentration and
  produced the round-robin/run-length fixes. This item is the cross-*host*
  analogue and must reuse its measurement style.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** (completed) — whole-set rotation with a run-length
  bound; establishes the "no new scheduler" precedent.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — post-dispatch cursor charge; how the
  previous fairness defect was diagnosed from decision logs.
- **WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW** (completed) — over-dispatch on a single-slot LLM:
  per-tick free-slot polling versus the proxy owner lease. Closest existing
  analysis of slot-vs-dispatch accounting.
- **WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA** (completed) — host-wide audit slot saturation from
  concurrent audits; the precedent that a shared proxy resource needs
  cross-instance coordination.
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** (completed) — proxy-owned audit budget: the one
  existing cross-machine serialisation pattern to imitate or extend.
- **WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T** (completed) — poller attribution on proxy:8000;
  produced the `client_ip` logging this measurement depends on.
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** (completed) — dispatch logs/leases on the remote
  host filesystem; where per-host dispatch evidence lives.
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** (completed) — truthful per-slot capacity consumption
  (`lease_state` / `capacity_hint`), the semantics of "a slot" in this codebase.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across
  multiple projects not working; the earlier defect family this item must not
  re-litigate for the per-host case.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** (completed) — docs for the enforced fair-scheduling
  rule and its metric; the documented-metric precedent to follow.
- **llm-manager `LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88`** (proxy) — client-identity logging
  (completed proxy side); the attribution prerequisite.
- **docs**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (host budget, proxy-derived audit
  admission, free-slot gate), `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime settings),
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` and
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/contention-queue-*.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was dispatched automatically by the herdr downtime worker
(`herdr-downtime`, session id recorded on the work item), so no interactive
producer round was available. Questions are recorded below with the documented
assumption used and marked for producer confirmation at review; none of them
blocks the investigation this item scopes.

- Q: What exactly is a "slot" here — the shared llama-proxy local-GPU slots, or
  the per-host dispatch opportunity on the shared backlog?
  — Assumption A1 (agent, from repo evidence): the shared **proxy local slots**
  (llama-server slots / local dispatch leases). Rationale: "slot" is used that
  way throughout `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` ("free-slot gate", "slot
  budget", `lease_state`), the dispatch budget is already per-host, and the only
  resource that is genuinely shared across hosts is the proxy GPU. AC1 requires
  measuring **both** slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host, so the
  analysis identifies the real contention point instead of assuming it.
  Source: repo search (`packages/herdr/src`, `llm-manager/proxy`).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Is the deliverable a report with proposed solutions, or a code change?
  — Answer (agent, from the item description): the description says "examine why
  this is and present potential solutions", so the deliverable is an
  evidence-backed RCA plus an options paper with one recommendation; the
  code change is recorded as follow-up work items. Source: item description.
  Status: accepted; revisit at review if the producer wants the fix in scope.
- Q: Must the fix be dispatcher-side (herdr) only, or may it require a proxy
  change in `llm-manager`?
  — Assumption A2 (agent): both may be proposed, but at least one option must be
  dispatcher-side, and any proxy change must be split into its own `LP-` item
  because this is a `WL-` (ContextHub) work item and the repos are separate.
  Source: repo boundary evidence (`llm-manager` has its own `LP-` worklog).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: How should "fair" be weighted when hosts have different numbers of
  dispatcher instances (and possibly different capacity)?
  — Assumption A3 (agent): the invariant to hold is that a host's share must
  **not** scale with its instance count; equal-share-per-host is the baseline,
  with capacity-weighting presented as an explicit alternative. The options paper
  quantifies both. Source: item description ("different machines may have
  different numbers of the dispatcher running").
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Which hosts and which proxy are in scope for the measurement?
  — Assumption A4 (agent): the ContextHub hosts that dispatch to the shared
  proxy (default `downtimeProxyUrl` `http://192.168.0.199:8000`) and any remote
  host whose `client_ip` appears in proxy logs during the window. Source:
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (proxy default), WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T (remote host
  evidence). Status: recorded; the window is chosen in the report.

Define "fair" for cross-host slot distribution and present at least two candidate solutions with trade-offs, failure modes, and fail-open behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Planning Complete — decomposition

Decomposed into six dependency-ordered investigation features (linear chain, measurement first):

| # | Work item | Feature | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WL-0MWO36PZ800887BI | Per-host measurement: collect and verify slot usage data | — |
| 2 | WL-0MWO37XKC000FUKF | Root-cause analysis: identify mechanisms causing slot imbalance | #1 |
| 3 | WL-0MWO388IQ001XKEW | Fairness definition and candidate solutions paper | #2 |
| 4 | WL-0MWO38JCR0086L3P | Recommendation: smallest change for host-independent share | #3 |
| 5 | WL-0MWO38U4W002853V | Publish fairness report and update documentation | #4 |
| 6 | WL-0MWO39PD6007MW65 | Verification: audit report claims and gate preservation | #5 |

Vertical-slice note: this item ships **no behaviour change** (an investigation whose deliverable is a report), so the slices are evidence → cause → options → decision → publication → audit. Each slice still crosses all layers: measurement includes a script + unit test + reproduction docs; publication includes docs + links + full test suite; verification re-audits claims, gates and tests. Phasing between slices: each downstream item's description is reviewed and updated using the previous slice's findings before it starts.

### Reused, not rebuilt

- `host-dispatch-budget.ts` machine-scoped ledger and `dispatch-budget.log` — the existing per-host accounting and audit trail.
- `host-budget-status.ts` read-only reductions — the existing per-host observability surface.
- `downtime-worker.fairness.ts` per-project rotation + decision-log evidence — the "no new scheduler" precedent to imitate.
- Proxy `client_ip` logging (LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88) — the existing host-attribution seam for measurement.

### Six automated review stages

Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: verified all nine parent acceptance criteria map to exactly one owning feature; no invented requirements. Where a parent AC is the feature's own deliverable, the child AC restates it (per-host measurement → #1; RCA mechanisms (a)–(d) → #2; fairness definition + two options → #3; recommendation + gate preservation → #4; documentation + test suite → #5; validation reproducibility → #1 and #6). Added one AC to #2 for the leader-election interaction (one poller per machine), which is a real gap in mechanism (b) coverage — no intent change.
Finished Completeness review: every feature has Goal, Acceptance Criteria, Deliverables and Key Files. `validate_key_files_format` passes for the parent and all six children. Added `**Key Files:**` to all six children (none existed); each cited path verified to exist in this repo, except `llm-manager/*` paths which are the documented cross-repo boundary and `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md` which the plan creates.
Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: dependencies form a strict chain #1 → #2 → #3 → #4 → #5 → #6 matching the investigation order; no cycles, no orphan. Test-first ordering is honoured where it applies (measurement helper unit test inside #1, the test-first slice). #6 intentionally runs last: a report's claims cannot be audited before the report exists — rationale recorded in the item.
Finished Scope sizing review: six features for a Medium-effort (17h expected, 26h recommended) investigation is proportionate — each is a single deliverable increment (one table, one RCA, one options paper, one recommendation, one report, one audit). No feature is a thin horizontal layer; no child merges two slices.
Finished Acceptance & testability review: every AC is pass/fail checkable (a table exists with named columns; mechanisms (a)–(d) each marked found or ruled out with a file reference; at least two options with named component/failure mode/fail-open/proxy-change verdict; one recommendation with linked follow-ups; queries reproduce each claim; gate list inspected). No vague criteria promoted or weakened.
Finished Polish & handoff review: each child states goal, ACs, deliverables and key files; the parent AC coverage review returns `proceed` with 0 uncovered ACs. Handoff is copy-pasteable: `wl next` on the parent leads to #1, the only unblocked child.

### AC coverage review

`apply_coverage_review(WL-0MWNYIL3Y0093GY0, target_stage="plan_complete")` → `action: proceed`, `advanced: true`, 0 created children, 0 conflicts. All nine parent ACs covered.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This plan ran as an automatically dispatched downtime session (`herdr-downtime`), so no interactive producer round was available. Questions below carry the documented assumption used and are marked for producer confirmation at review. **None blocks starting the investigation** — every one is answered by the parent acceptance criteria themselves, which the intake did not yet have.

- Q: What exactly is a "slot" — the shared llama-proxy local-GPU slots, or the per-host dispatch opportunity on the shared backlog?
  — Assumption A1 (agent, from repo evidence): the shared **proxy local slots**. Corroborated by parent AC1, which requires "local slot-seconds held" and "active vs. retained (idle) lease time" — proxy lease vocabulary. Source: parent AC1, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts`.
  Status: assumption retained; **confirm at review**.
- Q: Must the fix be dispatcher-side (herdr) only, or may it require a proxy change in `llm-manager`?
  — Assumption A2 (agent): both may be proposed; at least one option must be dispatcher-side, and any proxy change becomes its own `LP-` item. Corroborated by parent AC4 ("the options must include at least one that works without a proxy change") and the parent Constraints ("Cross-repo boundary"). Source: parent AC4 + Constraints; `llm-manager` is a separate repo with an `LP-` worklog.
  Status: assumption retained; **confirm at review**.
- Q: How should "fair" be weighted when hosts have different numbers of dispatcher instances (and possibly different capacity)?
  — Assumption A3 (agent): the invariant is that a host's share must **not** scale with its instance count; equal-share-per-host is the baseline, with capacity-weighting presented as an explicit quantified alternative. **Confirmed by parent AC3**, which states the invariant verbatim and requires documenting the capacity case and the no-dispatchable-work case. Source: parent AC3.
  Status: confirmed by the item's own AC; recommendation feature (#4) implements the choice.
- Q: Which hosts and which proxy are in scope for the measurement?
  — Assumption A4 (agent): the ContextHub hosts that dispatch to the shared proxy (default `downtimeProxyUrl` `http://192.168.0.199:8000`) plus any remote host whose `client_ip` appears in proxy logs during the window. Parent AC1 requires "at least two participating hosts". Source: `packages/herdr/README.md`, WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T.
  Status: assumption retained; the window is chosen in feature #1 and documented there.
- Q: Does the deliverable ship any code?
  — Answer: **no behaviour change in this item** (parent "Desired change" and "Scope-creep guard"). Implementation is recorded as linked follow-up items in feature #4. Measurement helper scripts are permitted (parent AC6 requires their unit test) but must run off-log, never in the dispatch loop (parent Constraints, hot-path budget).
  Source: parent "Desired change", "Constraints", "Risks and assumptions".

## OPEN QUESTION (producer) — `wl sync` skipped: shared worklog ref appears to have been reset

The plan is complete on this work item, but the final skill step (`wl sync`) was
**deliberately not run**. Evidence:

| Check | Value |
|---|---|
| Local SQLite store | 4744 work items, 20897 comments |
| Local `refs/worklog/data` | last synced 2026-09-19, 9631 JSONL lines |
| Remote `origin refs/worklog/data` | `09a07eb6a`, 2026-11-19T21:01:42Z, **100 work items + 3 comments** |
| `wl sync --dry-run` | "Remote state: 100 work items, 3 comments" → 91 updated, 4653 unchanged, total 4744 |

So a real `wl sync` from this host would push ~4.6k work items and ~20.9k
comments onto a ref that another host replaced with a 100-item store about 45
minutes before this session started. Two readings are possible:

1. **Accidental wipe** — a host ran `wl init`/`wl import` on a fresh store and
   synced, replacing the shared ref (AGENTS.md: "`wl import` is **destructive** —
   it replaces the entire store"). A sync from here is then the documented
   recovery: restore local → remote.
2. **Deliberate reset** — the 100-item store is the new intended baseline. A
   sync from here would re-pollute it with 4.6k resurrected items.

Because the two readings have opposite consequences and the decision is
store-wide (not scoped to this work item), it is left to the producer.

**Recommended action (producer):** determine which host pushed `09a07eb6a` and
whether the 100-item store was intentional. If accidental, run `wl sync` from a
host holding the full store (this one qualifies) or restore from
`.worklog/backups/worklog.db.2026-11-19T121836` (109 MB, 2026-11-19T12:18Z) per
the AGENTS.md recovery procedure.

**Consequence for this plan:** the six child items and the planning comment
created by this session exist only in the local SQLite store until a sync runs.
Nothing in the plan is invalidated by the delay — the children are unblocked and
dispatchable locally.
